builtinPersona.accessibility.name: Accessibility Auditor
builtinPersona.accessibility.summary: Audits real screens against WCAG by using them with a keyboard and a screen reader, not by reading an automated score.
builtinPersona.ai-search.name: AI Search Optimizer
builtinPersona.ai-search.summary: Makes pages easy for AI answer engines to quote correctly: direct answers, clear entities, sourced claims and matching structured data.
builtinPersona.analytics.name: Analytics Reporter
builtinPersona.analytics.summary: Answers questions from real data with queries committed to the repository, stating the denominator, the period and what is unknown rather than zero.
builtinPersona.api-tester.name: API Tester
builtinPersona.api-tester.summary: Validates an API's real behavior at its boundary — contracts, inputs, auth and errors — run against the actual endpoint rather than assumed from the code.
builtinPersona.architect.name: Architect
builtinPersona.architect.summary: Plans Epics by naming the trade-offs, boundaries, order and risks, and writes a plan a reviewer can prove wrong.
builtinPersona.backend.name: Backend Engineer
builtinPersona.backend.summary: Builds daemon, API and storage features with explicit contracts, safe migrations, bounded resources and typed errors.
builtinPersona.brand-guardian.name: Brand Guardian
builtinPersona.brand-guardian.summary: Keeps voice, name, logo, colour and typography consistent across the repository's pages and copy, from the project's own brand sources; flags drift and never invents a brand.
builtinPersona.code-reviewer.name: Code Reviewer
builtinPersona.code-reviewer.summary: Reviews diffs and plans against the real code, with ranked findings that each carry evidence and a concrete change.
builtinPersona.content-writer.name: Content Writer
builtinPersona.content-writer.summary: Drafts articles as files in the site's own format and voice, outline first, with verified facts and first-hand detail instead of filler.
builtinPersona.customer-success.name: Customer Success Manager
builtinPersona.customer-success.summary: Writes onboarding docs, health signals from real data, renewal and risk notes, and playbooks as files; proposes actions and never contacts customers.
builtinPersona.devops.name: DevOps Automator
builtinPersona.devops.summary: Removes manual steps from build, test and deploy by scripting them into the repository's own tooling, with verification and rollback built in.
builtinPersona.devrel.name: Developer Advocate
builtinPersona.devrel.summary: Writes quickstarts, samples, tutorials and changelogs that actually run, and turns developer friction into issues with evidence.
builtinPersona.email.name: Email Strategist
builtinPersona.email.summary: Drafts newsletters and email sequences into files, one goal per email, with honest subject lines, a plain-text version, checked links and a working unsubscribe.
builtinPersona.evidence-collector.name: Evidence Collector
builtinPersona.evidence-collector.summar: Captures proof for each claim — screenshots, logs, command output, measurements — and rules PASS or FAIL claim by claim, defaulting to FAIL until the evidence shows otherwise.
builtinPersona.feedback-synthesizer.name: Feedback Synthesizer
builtinPersona.feedback-synthesizer.summ: Reads the feedback actually available in the repository and its linked channels, and turns it into themes a plan can act on.
builtinPersona.finops.name: FinOps Engineer
builtinPersona.finops.summary: Makes spend traceable to a team and service before touching it, clears out waste first, and only then considers any long-term commitment.
builtinPersona.frontend.name: Frontend Engineer
builtinPersona.frontend.summary: Builds web console features that work at phone width, are accessible, and handle loading, error and empty states.
builtinPersona.growth.name: Growth Hacker
builtinPersona.growth.summary: Turns growth ideas into stated hypotheses and small, reversible, measurable changes, using the site's real data and never dark patterns.
builtinPersona.image-prompt.name: Image Prompt Engineer
builtinPersona.image-prompt.summary: Writes image-generation prompts as files in the repository, matched to the brand and the page each image serves, with alt text; the person picks the result.
builtinPersona.incident-commander.name: Incident Commander
builtinPersona.incident-commander.summar: Runs an active incident to a verified, stable resolution with an accurate timeline, then turns it into a blameless report with owned follow-ups.
builtinPersona.instagram.name: Instagram Curator
builtinPersona.instagram.summary: Drafts Instagram posts, carousels and grid plans from the project's own material and assets, with plain captions, restrained hashtags and alt text.
builtinPersona.minimal-change.name: Minimal-Change Engineer
builtinPersona.minimal-change.summary: Fixes the stated bug with the smallest change in behaviour, after reproducing it, adding a test that fails before the fix, and checking who else depends on the code it touches.
builtinPersona.performance.name: Performance Benchmarker
builtinPersona.performance.summary: Measures a system's real performance before and after a change, under a load it can defend, and reports the numbers with how they were produced.
builtinPersona.pr.name: PR & Communications
builtinPersona.pr.summary: Drafts press releases, announcements and media lists as files, with every claim fact-checked and nothing released without the person's approval.
builtinPersona.pricing.name: Pricing Analyst
builtinPersona.pricing.summary: Analyses pricing and packaging from real cost, usage and competitor data, states assumptions, sensitivity and trade-offs, and proposes rather than changes prices.
builtinPersona.privacy.name: Privacy & Compliance Officer
builtinPersona.privacy.summary: Maps the personal data the code collects, stores and sends, and checks retention, consent, access and the privacy notice against what the code actually does.
builtinPersona.product-manager.name: Product Manager
builtinPersona.product-manager.summary: Turns a request into a checked problem statement, a scoped plan and named acceptance checks, then keeps the team aligned as scope moves.
builtinPersona.reality-checker.name: Reality Checker
builtinPersona.reality-checker.summary: Verifies claims with runs, logs and screenshots; everything is "not yet proven" until evidence says otherwise.
builtinPersona.secrets.name: Secrets & Credentials Engineer
builtinPersona.secrets.summary: Owns secrets from creation to revocation, keeps them out of code and logs, prefers short-lived credentials, and treats any leak as live until rotated at the source.
builtinPersona.security.name: Security Engineer
builtinPersona.security.summary: Finds and fixes risks at trust boundaries, covering auth and pairing, secrets, input validation and blast radius.
builtinPersona.seo.name: SEO Specialist
builtinPersona.seo.summary: Fixes real pages so search engines understand them: titles, descriptions, headings, links, structured data and speed, checked in the built output.
builtinPersona.social-media.name: Social Media Strategist
builtinPersona.social-media.summary: Plans and drafts platform-specific posts and a posting calendar into files, adapted from existing content, and never posts anything itself.
builtinPersona.sprint-prioritizer.name: Sprint Prioritizer
builtinPersona.sprint-prioritizer.summar: Orders a backlog of Issues by evidence of value and cost, and states what will not fit before the round starts.
builtinPersona.sre.name: Site Reliability Engineer
builtinPersona.sre.summary: Treats reliability as a measured budget, defining SLOs from real signals, alerts that page on user impact, and turning repeated manual fixes into automation.
builtinPersona.support.name: Support Responder
builtinPersona.support.summary: Drafts replies and help articles grounded in the product's actual behaviour, reproduces reported issues and files bugs with evidence; drafts only, never sends.
builtinPersona.technical-writer.name: Technical Writer
builtinPersona.technical-writer.summary: Writes docs for the reader in front of them, problem first, with examples that run and text in sync with code.
builtinPersona.test-automation.name: Test Automation Engineer
builtinPersona.test-automation.summary: Builds deterministic automated suites for the journeys that matter, kills flake at the root cause, and leaves every failure debuggable from evidence alone.
builtinPersona.trend-researcher.name: Trend Researcher
builtinPersona.trend-researcher.summary: Researches what is publicly documented about a market or technology trend, cites every source, and separates signal from speculation.
builtinPersona.ui-designer.name: UI Designer
builtinPersona.ui-designer.summary: Designs screens and components in the codebase's own design system: tokens, every state, both themes, phone width and readable contrast, verified by screenshots.
builtinPersona.ui-finish-gate.name: UI Finish Gate
builtinPersona.ui-finish-gate.summary: The last check before a visible change ships: real screenshots at phone and desktop width, both themes, every state, overflow, alignment and focus, plus whether the screen reads as this product rather than any product; fails by default until the evidence supports a pass.
builtinPersona.ux-architect.name: UX Architect
builtinPersona.ux-architect.summary: Designs information architecture, flows, layout systems and component structure a developer can build, following the person's whole journey including failure paths.
builtinPersona.ux-researcher.name: UX Researcher
builtinPersona.ux-researcher.summary: Runs research that fits inside a repository, reading the product's actual UI code, prior tickets and any given transcripts, to find real usability issues.
builtinPersona.zero-review-lead.name: Zero-based Review Lead
builtinPersona.zero-review-lead.summary: Owns a review Epic, assembles role reviewers, and turns their evidence into a target design.
builtinPersona.zh-editor.name: Chinese Editor
builtinPersona.zh-editor.summary: Writes, rewrites or restructures a whole Chinese article from its reader, one-sentence point and heading outline down, so it reads as thought in Chinese rather than translated.

capacityRow.antigravity.ancestry_rows.fu: An incomplete or longer chain cannot establish identity.
capacityRow.antigravity.ancestry_rows.wh: Limits the process ancestry inspected to verify one native hook.
New conversation mappings are refused when full; existing history is retained.
Limits native conversation mappings to their original workspace and context.
capacityRow.antigravity.context_index_by: A full index refuses the transaction and retains the last committed state.
Limits the private durable index of launches, native history and prepared receipts.
capacityRow.antigravity.context_receipts: New receipts are refused when full; a prepared receipt never proves delivery or loading.
Limits prepared context receipts to the latest service sequence per launch.
capacityRow.antigravity.first_input_slot: New reservations are refused when full. Consumed slots are retained to prevent duplicate input.
Limits durable first-input reservations to one per launch; restart never restores execution authority.
capacityRow.antigravity.hook_config_byte: Oversized configuration is refused; unrelated settings are preserved.
Limits the existing and merged workspace hook configuration.
capacityRow.antigravity.acp_sessions.wha: Keeps one personal Antigravity preview process on this machine.
capacityRow.antigravity.acp_sessions.ful: Close the current preview Session before opening another.
Bounds each private ACP protocol frame and personal-settings read.
An oversized frame stops this process; its prompt is never retried automatically.
capacityRow.antigravity.acp_view_bytes.w: Bounds each Gemini history page and the in-memory preview.
capacityRow.antigravity.acp_view_bytes.f: Older entries remain saved on disk and can be read on earlier pages.
capacityRow.antigravity.history_connecti: Limits the shared SQLite connection used for saved Gemini history.
History reads wait for the connection within their request deadline; saved entries are kept.
capacityRow.antigravity.acp_call_seconds: Bounds each native ACP call, including a model turn.
The owned process is stopped at the deadline; uncertain input is never replayed.
capacityRow.antigravity.hook_connections: A full service refuses the connection with a busy error; existing work retains its deadline.
Limits active local Antigravity hook connections; there is no work queue.
capacityRow.antigravity.hook_frame_bytes: An oversized frame is refused before allocating its declared body.
Limits the whole local hook request or response frame, including launch metadata.
capacityRow.antigravity.hook_payload_byt: Oversized input is refused before it can establish a Session identity.
Limits one local hook payload or launch capability read.
capacityRow.antigravity.hook_request_sec: The connection closes at the deadline. A timeout never produces a successful native response.
Limits one local hook request, including process verification and response composition.
capacityRow.antigravity.hook_timeout_sec: The native hook stops waiting at the deadline; this is not proof a model or tool ran.
Limits the hook command duration installed by Clawdline.
capacityRow.antigravity.launch_context_b: Oversized context is refused before a process can open; no content is truncated.
Limits each immutable role, Board language and Project memory context document.
capacityRow.antigravity.live_bindings.fu: New identities are refused when full; an existing identity is never silently replaced.
capacityRow.antigravity.live_bindings.wh: Limits distinct live process identities retained by the hook bridge.
capacityRow.antigravity.managed_launches: New commitments are refused when full; existing launch ownership stays intact.
Limits trusted managed launch commitments independently of live observations.
capacityRow.antigravity.native_process_f: Oversized kernel data is refused before it can establish process identity.
Limits each kernel process pseudo-file read.
capacityRow.antigravity.native_tty_entri: An incomplete or oversized device listing cannot establish terminal identity.
Limits direct device entries inspected to resolve a controlling terminal.
capacityRow.antigravity.observation_byte: A full snapshot refuses the new observation and retains the previous verified state.
Limits the saved snapshot of verified Antigravity observations.
capacityRow.antigravity.process_read_sec: A timeout leaves identity unknown and cannot authorize a Session operation.
Limits one process identity or ancestry verification operation.
capacityRow.antigravity.retention_second: Expired observations are reclaimed at the next observation, not by a background deletion timer.
Limits the age of observations retained by the bridge; cleanup runs on new input.
capacityRow.antigravity.saved_launches.f: New launches are refused when full; original resumable contexts are retained.
capacityRow.antigravity.saved_launches.w: Limits durable Antigravity launch slots, including interrupted preparations.
capacityRow.antigravity.state_age_second: State becomes unknown after expiry; identity alone cannot authorize sending.
Limits how long a verified native observation can describe the current interactive state.
capacityRow.artifacts.drops.full: The oldest pictures are deleted whatever their age. Pictures older than a week are cleaned up anyway. If an assistant later cannot open an old picture, send it again.
capacityRow.artifacts.drops.what: The total size of pictures you sent into a conversation, saved as files for the terminal program to open. They must outlive the send because a Session may read them again after resuming.
capacityRow.artifacts.drops_young.full: You get a push notification. A conversation that tries to reread that picture, for example after resuming, cannot open it; send the picture again if it is asked for.
capacityRow.artifacts.drops_young.what: Whether, in the last day, the size ceiling on pictures you sent into conversations deleted one that was less than a day old. Any at all means that space is too small for how you use it.
capacityRow.artifacts.image_bytes.full: Whichever ceiling is reached first, by count or by size, removes the oldest picture, and Clawdline says why where it appeared. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.artifacts.image_bytes.what: The total size of the pictures assistants sent to show you in replies. This is the second ceiling on the same pictures, so a few very large images cannot fill the disk.
capacityRow.artifacts.images.full: The oldest picture is removed to make room; where it appeared, Clawdline says it was removed to make room rather than showing a broken image. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.artifacts.images.what: How many pictures Clawdline holds that assistants sent to show you in a reply. Each picture also expires after a day on its own, so this ceiling only matters when many arrive at once.
capacityRow.artifacts.report_image_pixel: An image beyond this limit is omitted from the report. Resize it before embedding it again; the rest of the report remains readable.
The decoded pixel count of one screenshot embedded in an HTML report. This limits image memory independently of the document byte limit.
An image beyond this limit is omitted from the report. The author can resize the screenshot and publish the report again.
The longest side of one screenshot embedded in an HTML report. The ceiling stops a tiny compressed file from expanding into an excessively large image.
capacityRow.artifacts.report_total_image: Images beyond the remaining report budget are omitted. Resize or reduce the screenshots before publishing again; text and earlier valid images remain readable.
The combined decoded pixel count of all screenshots retained in one HTML report. This also counts repeated images, so a small file cannot allocate unlimited image memory.
capacityRow.audit.security.full: The current file is closed and a new one begins; the old files stay on disk because Clawdline never deletes them. Nothing stops working. If disk space matters, you can archive or remove the old files yourself.
capacityRow.audit.security.what: The security log of who may reach this machine: device pairings, password sign-ins, push destinations and schedules set up remotely. Nothing in it is ever deleted, so it is split into files to keep each one small enough to open.
capacityRow.artifacts.video_bytes.full: The video is refused before transfer. Export a smaller MP4 and publish it again.
capacityRow.artifacts.video_bytes.what: The size of one published MP4 video. The limit bounds the complete video kept in browser memory for playback.
The reader only requests bounded chunks. An invalid chunk is refused and playback stops.
Video bytes in one encrypted read. Sequential chunks leave the Cloud connection available for other work.
capacityRow.board.receipts.full: A new change would be refused with a try-again-later answer until the oldest record ages out; no record is dropped early. In practice this is hard to reach. Wait and try again.
capacityRow.board.receipts.what: Records of the last day's Board switches (turning the Board on or off, and consent to AI summaries), kept so a request resent after a network hiccup is not applied twice.
capacityRow.cache.assistant_quota.full: It has only ever held a couple of entries, so in practice it does not fill. If it did, the oldest reading would be dropped and read again from the files; nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.assistant_quota.what: What Claude, Codex and other assistants last reported about your plan's usage windows, held for a few seconds per assistant. It is read from files the assistants already write, so it grows only with the number of assistants.
capacityRow.cache.background_agents.full: The oldest remembered entries are forgotten and the files are read again when needed. At worst agent details appear a moment later. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.background_agents.what: How much Clawdline remembers about Claude's background agents and their files, so it does not reread every agent's files each time a conversation row refreshes.
capacityRow.cache.git_not_repo.full: When time is up Git is asked again. If you just ran git init in such a folder, its Git details may take up to this long to appear; nothing else to do.
capacityRow.cache.git_not_repo.what: How long Clawdline remembers that a folder is not a Git repository, so it does not run Git there again on every refresh. Only this not-a-repository answer is remembered.
capacityRow.cache.git_not_repo_rows.full: The folder remembered longest ago is forgotten, and the next look at it runs Git once more. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.git_not_repo_rows.what: How many folders known not to be Git repositories Clawdline remembers at once. Without a ceiling, a machine with many such folders would keep growing this list in memory.
capacityRow.cache.image_thumbs.full: The preview used longest ago is dropped and redrawn the next time it is needed, so it may appear a moment later. The images themselves are never lost; nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.image_thumbs.what: Small preview images shown on Board cards and to-do rows, kept ready so they are not redrawn from the full image every time a page opens. Holding every one would keep growing memory.
capacityRow.cache.pinned_read.full: This is a freshness window, not storage. If the last check is older, a fresh scan is taken first, so that phone view may take a few seconds longer to open. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.pinned_read.what: When your phone opens a conversation's transcript, info, Git or to-dos through Cloud, Clawdline first checks it is still the same running Session. A check finished within this many seconds is reused instead of rescanning every terminal.
capacityRow.cache.provider_quota.full: The newest reading replaces that service’s previous snapshot; no Session or project adds another entry.
capacityRow.cache.provider_quota.what: Keeps one provider quota snapshot per supported service.
capacityRow.cache.provider_quota_refresh: Repeated refreshes reuse the cached result; a provider cooldown can extend the wait.
Sets the minimum gap between provider quota checks.
capacityRow.cache.provider_quota_request: A slow check ends without blocking the interface and keeps the last reading marked outdated.
Limits the total time for one provider quota refresh.
capacityRow.cache.provider_quota_respons: Oversized input is refused; the last successful quota remains marked outdated.
Limits each credential file and quota response read.
capacityRow.cache.reclaim_summary.full: This is a refresh interval, not storage. The cleanup summary may be up to this old; nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.reclaim_summary.what: How long the machine dashboard reuses its summary of worktree cleanup (how many were kept and why) before reading it again. The dashboard refreshes every few seconds, and recounting each time would load the data file for nothing.
capacityRow.cache.session_activity.full: The conversation read longest ago is forgotten and its record is opened again on the next refresh. Nothing visible; nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.session_activity.what: What Clawdline last learned about each Session's own conversation record: where it is and when its newest turn happened. It lets a list that redraws every two seconds avoid reopening each record unless it changed.
capacityRow.cache.session_execution_memo: With more conversations than this, the list is simply not remembered and is checked against the database every time, as before; you see no difference. Nothing for you to do.
Clawdline remembers the last list of open conversations it checked, so an unchanged list, rebuilt every couple of seconds while a page is open, does not write to the database each time.
capacityRow.cache.session_inventory.full: When time is up, that terminal's Sessions show their state as unknown until it answers again. Usually this clears by itself; if it persists, iTerm2 may be stuck or missing automation permission.
capacityRow.cache.session_inventory.what: How long the Session list keeps showing the last complete list from a terminal (such as iTerm2) that failed to answer this time. It stops one slow iTerm2 from turning every row into unknown, without passing off an old reading as current.
capacityRow.cache.session_links.full: The project whose links were looked at longest ago is forgotten; next time its sheet opens it takes a moment longer. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.session_links.what: How many projects' Links sheets (repository, deploy, servers) Clawdline keeps ready. Building one runs Git and reads several files, taking a few hundred milliseconds, so remembered answers make the sheet open at once.
capacityRow.cache.session_project_keys.f: Past this many folders, the one checked longest ago is forgotten and looked up again the next time a Session works there; you see no difference. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.session_project_keys.w: Clawdline remembers which Project each Session's folder belongs to for half a minute, so the Session list, rebuilt every couple of seconds, does not look through the folders again each time.
capacityRow.cache.session_skills.full: The list used longest ago is forgotten and rescanned the next time you open that menu, which may take a moment longer. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.session_skills.what: The list of skills shown in a Session's slash (/) menu, remembered per folder and assistant for a few minutes so typing / doesn't rescan the skills folders each time.
capacityRow.cache.source_answer.full: Past this age that terminal's rows show as unverified until the refresh finishes, then return to normal. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.source_answer.what: How old one terminal's last complete answer may be and still count as current while the Session list is refreshing. Without it, every row looked unverified for the whole time a slow iTerm2 refresh ran.
capacityRow.cache.terminal_screens.full: The screen asked about longest ago is dropped, as is one nobody has asked about for two minutes; that row's line returns after its next capture. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.terminal_screens.what: The last captured terminal screen for each Session the list has asked about, used to show each row's latest line and menu without capturing the terminal every time the list redraws.
capacityRow.cache.transcript_titles.full: The least recently used titles are forgotten and read again from the file when needed. At worst a title shows a moment later. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cache.transcript_titles.what: How many conversation titles Clawdline remembers, so the Session list does not reread the end of every conversation file each time it refreshes.
capacityRow.callback.args.full: This is a ceiling on one command. One with more words is refused and nothing is started; the Session is told and can wrap the command in a script.
capacityRow.callback.args.what: How many words the command may have when a Session hands a long-running command, such as a deploy, to Clawdline to run and wake it when it finishes. A cap keeps a malformed request from starting something unexpected.
capacityRow.callback.command_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one command. A longer one is refused and nothing is started; the Session is told and can put the command in a script.
capacityRow.callback.command_bytes.what: How long, in total, the command may be when a Session hands a long-running command to Clawdline to run and be woken when it finishes. It stops one request from carrying a huge command line.
capacityRow.callback.output_bytes.full: When it passes, the log is cleared except for its last part, with a first line saying earlier output was dropped, and the command keeps writing. The end of the output, which decides the result, is kept.
capacityRow.callback.output_bytes.what: How much output a handed-off background command may write to its log file while it runs. A noisy command left running would otherwise fill the disk.
capacityRow.callback.per_machine.full: A further one is refused and not started; the Session that asked is told and can try again once another finishes. Nothing for you to do unless commands seem stuck.
capacityRow.callback.per_machine.what: How many handed-off background commands, from all Sessions together, may run on this machine at once. Each is a real process using CPU and memory, so a cap keeps them from crowding out your own work.
capacityRow.callback.per_root.full: A further one is refused and not started; the Session is told and can wait for one of its running commands to finish. These do not take a child task's slot.
capacityRow.callback.per_root.what: How many of those handed-off commands one top-level Session may have running at once. It stops one conversation from filling this machine with background commands.
capacityRow.callback.tail_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one read. Only the last lines that fit go into the finish notice; the rest of the output stays in the log file for anyone who wants it. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.callback.tail_bytes.what: How much of the end of a finished background command's log is read to tell the Session how it went. Reading only the end keeps that finish notice short.
capacityRow.cloud.content_key_epoch_reco: A larger record is not read; the epoch stays unknown and owner diagnostics are not sealed until the device is paired again.
How large the record of this machine's content-key epoch may be.
capacityRow.cloud.envelope_key_id.full: An oversized key identifier is refused before an envelope is sent or opened.
capacityRow.cloud.envelope_key_id.what: An encrypted envelope key identifier is limited to 128 bytes, including the epoch and full content-key hash.
capacityRow.cloud.header_read_diagnostic: The oldest steps are dropped as new ones come; the copy simply covers the most recent ones. They live only in that tab and the machine cannot count them; nothing for you to do.
How many steps of reading a Session's to-dos and needs-your-attention header a browser tab keeps, without content, for the copy-diagnostics button on this Status page. It keeps that copy short.
When time is up, older steps are left out of the copy and dropped at the next save. Nothing for you to do.
How long a browser tab keeps those Session-header reading steps for the copy-diagnostics button. Old steps would only confuse a report about what is happening now.
capacityRow.cloud.health_active_slots.fu: A new step is still carried out but not tracked; the connection health record says its coverage is partial for that period.
capacityRow.cloud.health_active_slots.wh: How many in-progress connection steps this machine tracks at once, so it can tell which one stopped moving without keeping an unbounded list.
capacityRow.cloud.health_capture_budget_: No new capture starts until it finishes, and the health status says the capture worker is unavailable.
How long a stall capture may take before it is called unavailable.
capacityRow.cloud.health_capture_export_: Goroutines are left out from the end, the stalled one last, and the capture says it is truncated.
How large one cleaned stall capture may be in the health export.
The other frames are counted, not kept.
How many frames of one goroutine a stall capture keeps.
capacityRow.cloud.health_capture_raw_byt: The dump is cut off and the capture says it is truncated; it is never saved or sent.
How large the one raw goroutine dump of a stall capture may be.
capacityRow.cloud.health_captures_per_mi: A later stall is recorded as usual but not captured; the refusal is counted.
How many stall captures may start in one minute.
capacityRow.cloud.health_investigation_b: Larger evidence is refused before acceptance; no investigation task starts.
The maximum size of one frozen incident evidence bundle read by this machine.
capacityRow.cloud.health_investigation_r: The read is canceled without accepting evidence or launching a task.
How long one leased incident evidence download may take.
An oversized report is refused; the task must submit a smaller valid report.
The maximum size of one typed investigation report from a task.
A report with more references is refused as a whole.
How many distinct stored health event references one investigation report may name.
capacityRow.cloud.health_journal_bytes.f: The oldest events are dropped and counted; a later reading says exactly which events are gone.
capacityRow.cloud.health_journal_bytes.w: How much memory the connection health events may use in total.
capacityRow.cloud.health_journal_rows.fu: The oldest events are dropped and counted; a later reading says exactly which events are gone.
capacityRow.cloud.health_journal_rows.wh: How many connection health events this machine keeps in memory, such as a step found stuck or recovered.
capacityRow.cloud.health_owner_incidents: The oldest stall is forgotten; its recovery is not added to the owner diagnostic, but the local export still has it.
How many stalls the owner diagnostics remember so a capture or recovery can be added to them.
capacityRow.cloud.health_pending_transit: A finding that does not fit is not kept; it is counted and the record says how many were lost.
How many connection health findings can wait to be written to the connection health record.
capacityRow.cloud.health_query_bytes.ful: The reading stops early, says it was cut short and gives the place to continue from.
capacityRow.cloud.health_query_bytes.wha: How much data one reading of connection health events returns.
capacityRow.cloud.health_query_rows.full: The reading stops early, says it was cut short and gives the place to continue from.
capacityRow.cloud.health_query_rows.what: How many connection health events one reading returns.
capacityRow.cloud.health_record_bytes.fu: An event that is too large is not kept and is counted as refused.
capacityRow.cloud.health_record_bytes.wh: The largest single connection health event, which only ever holds codes and identifiers.
A further loop step is carried out but not tracked, and is counted as a missed critical observation.
Tracking places kept for the loops that read, write and keep the connection alive, so ordinary requests cannot crowd them out.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_attempt_: The request is abandoned and counts as one failed attempt.
How long one upload of a sealed owner diagnostic may take.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_attempts: It stays waiting with the same bytes and is sent again later.
How many times one version of a sealed owner diagnostic is sent in a row.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_cipherte: A larger one is refused and not sent; nothing is cut short.
How large one sealed owner diagnostic may be once encrypted.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_life_sec: It expires in Cloud and its local record is removed.
How long Cloud keeps a sealed owner diagnostic after its first version.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_queued_j: The next one is refused at once and counted as dropped; nothing waits for room.
How many owner diagnostics may wait to be sealed at once.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_request_: A larger one is refused and not sent.
How large one upload of a sealed owner diagnostic may be.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_response: A longer answer is not taken as a receipt.
How much of Cloud's answer to a sealed upload is read.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_revision: No further version is made; the earlier ones stay as they were.
How many versions one sealed owner diagnostic may have.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_snapshot: A larger one is refused and not sent.
How large one owner diagnostic may be before it is encrypted.
The diagnostic is refused and not sent.
How many covered sources one owner diagnostic may name.
The diagnostic is refused and not sent.
How long any one text field of an owner diagnostic may be.
The rest are counted and the diagnostic says it is truncated.
How many frames of the stalled goroutine one owner diagnostic carries.
The rest are left out and the diagnostic says it is truncated.
How many exact source lines one owner diagnostic names for a stall.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_store_at: A new one is refused at once until an expired one is removed.
How many sealed owner diagnostics this machine keeps a local record of.
capacityRow.cloud.health_sealed_store_by: A new version is refused at once; nothing already kept is removed.
How much disk the local records of sealed owner diagnostics may use.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_bytes.ful: The oldest saved period is deleted and counted; readings show the earliest moment still kept instead of promising seven days.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_bytes.wha: How much disk space this machine's saved connection health history may use, so it can be read after a restart without filling the disk.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_dir_entri: Files past the limit are left untouched and the start-up check says it did not look at all of them.
How many files this machine looks at in the connection health history folder when it starts.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_frame_byt: An event that is too large is not saved and is counted; a saved entry claiming to be larger is treated as damaged.
How large one saved connection health event may be.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_lost_rang: The oldest group is forgotten; asking about events in it answers unknown rather than saved.
How many groups of unsaved connection health events this machine remembers, so it can answer whether a given event reached the disk.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_queue_byt: New events are not saved and are counted; the saved history marks how many were missed at that point.
How much connection health data waits in memory to be saved to disk.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_queue_row: New events are not saved and are counted; the saved history marks how many were missed at that point.
How many connection health events wait in memory to be saved to disk, so a slow disk never slows the connection itself.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_readers.f: Another reading is turned away at once and can be tried again; saving new events is never slowed.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_readers.w: How many readings of saved connection health history may run at the same time.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_seconds.f: Older history is deleted; readings show the earliest moment still kept.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_seconds.w: How long this machine keeps saved connection health history, so a problem from earlier in the week can still be looked up.
capacityRow.cloud.health_store_segment_b: The file is closed and a new one is started; nothing is lost.
How large one file of saved connection health history grows before a new file is started.
The oldest file is deleted and counted; readings show the earliest moment still kept.
How many files of saved connection health history are kept, so frequent restarts do not leave thousands of small files.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_attempt_: The attempt is stopped and tried again later; it never holds up anything else on this machine.
How long one connection health upload may take, from connecting to the answer.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_attempts: The upload is given up and counted; Cloud may or may not have kept it, and the status says that it is unknown.
How many times one upload of connection health evidence is tried before giving up.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_batch_by: Records are split across more uploads; a single record too large to send is counted as not sent instead of being cut short.
How large one upload of connection health evidence to Cloud may be.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_batch_ev: The rest waits, in order, for the next upload.
How many connection health records one upload to Cloud may carry.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_hourly_b: Uploading pauses until the next hour; nothing is thrown away, and the status says it is waiting for its budget.
How much connection health evidence this machine may send to Cloud in one hour, kept below what Cloud allows.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_hourly_r: Uploading pauses until the next hour and the status says so.
How many connection health uploads this machine may make to Cloud in one hour.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_receipts: The oldest receipt is forgotten; the counts of what was delivered are kept.
How many recent Cloud receipts for connection health uploads this machine keeps.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_response: A longer answer is not taken as a receipt, and the upload is tried again.
How much of Cloud's answer to a connection health upload is read.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_retry_af: A longer request is shortened to this wait.
The longest wait Cloud may ask for before the next connection health upload.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_retry_se: The upload is given up and counted, the same as after its last try.
How long one upload of connection health evidence keeps being retried.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_state_by: Progress is not saved and nothing is sent until it can be; the status says the file could not be written.
How large the file that remembers connection health upload progress may grow.
capacityRow.cloud.health_upload_step_pag: The rest is read in the next round.
How many pages of saved connection health history one upload round reads.
capacityRow.cloud.identity_pairing_decis: A larger request is refused before it is read; the pairing keeps waiting for a valid answer.
The size of this machine's answer to a diagnostics-key code comparison.
capacityRow.cloud.identity_pairing_poll_: The pairing stops and hands nothing over; start it again.
How many times this machine checks for the other device's next pairing step.
capacityRow.cloud.identity_pairing_run_s: The run stops and the Settings window says the link expired; nothing is handed over.
How long one diagnostics-key handover may run on this machine.
capacityRow.cloud.lane_refusals.full: Additional busy replies are counted as unsent and recorded in the log. Those requests may time out; commands continue through their own lane.
capacityRow.cloud.lane_refusals.what: How many machine-busy replies may wait to be sent, so a stalled reply cannot hold up the machine's command and read dispatch.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_body_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one message. A longer one is refused before it is sent and nothing goes out; shorten it or send a file path instead.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_body_bytes.what: How long a single Agent message or handoff sent to another machine may be. It has to fit, encrypted, in one Cloud transfer.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_discovery_reply.f: Duplicate replies are ignored; a timed-out query releases its reply slot.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_discovery_reply.w: Each inventory query retains one encrypted reply until its requesting Session reads it.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_frame_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one message. An outgoing one over it is not sent; an incoming one over it is ignored. Normal messages stay well under it because the text itself has a smaller ceiling.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_frame_bytes.what: How big one encrypted cross-machine message may be on its way through Cloud, including its signature and the message itself.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_grants.full: Cloud no longer creates these, so it should not fill. If it did, a new one would be refused while existing ones still work; the app has no way to clear them.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_grants.what: Older per-conversation permissions that let one Session on another machine reach a specific Session here. They are kept even after expiring or being revoked, as a record of what was allowed.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_inbox.full: New messages and handoffs from other machines are refused, and the sending machine is told so. Nothing removes old ones today, so cross-machine messaging stays blocked once full.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_inbox.what: Agent messages and Session handoffs received from your other machines. Each is kept as a record of what was asked of this machine and by whom.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_inbox_page.full: This is a ceiling on one read, not a store that fills. The next message comes with the next read. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_inbox_page.what: How many received cross-machine messages one encrypted read carries: one message with its delivery record, so a single read always fits through Cloud.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_ingress.full: Extra ones are dropped and noted in the log; the sending machine gets no answer for them and has to check again. You may see a cross-machine message arrive late or need resending.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_ingress.what: How many incoming cross-machine messages, task starts and status checks may wait while each is checked for permission, so a burst from another machine cannot stall this machine's Cloud connection.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_outbox.full: Sending anything new to another machine is refused. Nothing removes old records today, so cross-machine sending stays blocked once full.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_outbox.what: Agent messages, handoffs and task starts this machine has sent to your other machines, kept so Clawdline can later check whether each one arrived.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_pairs.full: Turning on access for another pair of machines is refused; existing pairs keep working. Switching a pair off does not free its slot, and the app currently has no way to clear old ones.
capacityRow.cloud.peer_pairs.what: How many machine-to-machine permissions this machine keeps, from the Cross-machine access switches in Cloud. Each one decides whether Sessions on two machines may message or hand off to each other, so none is dropped to make room.
capacityRow.cloud.read_queue.full: An additional read receives a machine-busy answer with a retry delay. Reads already waiting keep their place; commands use their own lane.
capacityRow.cloud.read_queue.what: How many Cloud reads may wait while this machine's eight read workers are occupied. A short burst waits here without holding up commands.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_body.full: Oversized exchanges are refused without decrypting or adopting a key.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_body.what: One signed content-key control message is limited to 4096 bytes before parsing.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_interval.full: Offers inside the interval are refused; viewers can retry after the interval.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_interval.what: This machine admits one raw key offer every two seconds across all viewers.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_lifetime.full: An expired exchange is refused; the viewer must create a fresh operation.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_lifetime.what: A pending content-key exchange expires within two minutes so an old signed request cannot remain usable indefinitely.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_pending.full: Additional offers are refused immediately; ordinary relay messages keep flowing.
capacityRow.cloud.rekey_pending.what: At most eight signed raw key exchanges may be running on this machine.
capacityRow.cloud.relay_queue.full: A new request is turned away with a machine-busy, try-again answer; requests already in line are still handled. You may need to tap again after a moment.
capacityRow.cloud.relay_queue.what: How many requests from the phone or Cloud page may wait to be handled on this machine at once, so a burst cannot pile up unbounded work while the machine is slow.
capacityRow.cloud.reload_stop_seconds.fu: If the old connection has not stopped by then, the new one is not started and the change reports an error. Try again; if it keeps failing, restart Clawdline.
capacityRow.cloud.reload_stop_seconds.wh: How long Clawdline waits for its old Cloud connection to shut down when you change Cloud settings, so two connections never run at once.
capacityRow.cloud.roster_short_read_atte: If every try fails, terminal and Session content access from Cloud stays closed until a later check succeeds; nothing is revoked. If it keeps happening, check this machine's network.

How many tries the machine makes, within the same short deadline, to read your account's device list. A second try on a fresh connection recovers a stuck network path without making the wait any longer.
capacityRow.cloud.session_row_asks.full: Further requests are told the machine is busy and to try again in a second; the page asks again. At worst a conversation's latest state appears a moment later.
capacityRow.cloud.session_row_asks.what: How many requests from the Cloud page for a single conversation's latest state may wait in line at once, so many open viewers cannot pile up unbounded work on this machine.
capacityRow.cloud.session_row_id_bytes.f: This is a ceiling on one request. A longer id is refused as malformed without being looked up. Ids from Clawdline never come near it, so there is nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cloud.session_row_id_bytes.w: How long a conversation id may be when the Cloud page asks this machine for one conversation's latest state. Real ids are a few dozen characters, so anything far longer is not one this machine issued.
capacityRow.cloud.session_row_volatile_s: Such small changes reach the phone up to this late; any real change, like a new state or a question, still goes at once. Nothing for you to do.

How often the phone's conversation list is resent when the only change is small: the last-activity time, background agents or token count. This keeps a busy conversation from using the phone's data every second.
capacityRow.cloud.spool.full: A new answer is refused and nothing already queued is dropped, so a phone request may be told this machine is busy or wait until it times out. It drains as Cloud catches up; if it stays full, check this machine's Cloud connection.
capacityRow.cloud.spool.what: How many answers this machine has sent toward your phone or the web console through Cloud that Cloud has not yet confirmed. If Cloud stops confirming, an unlimited queue would grow without end on this machine.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_bytes.full: Whichever of the count or size ceiling is crossed first refuses a new answer; the phone may be told this machine is busy or wait until it times out. It drains as Cloud confirms; if it stays full, check the Cloud connection.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_bytes.what: The total size of the same unconfirmed answers waiting to go out through Cloud to your phone or web console. A few large ones, such as images or documents, can use up memory long before the count does.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_channel_bytes.fu: This is the ceiling that usually refuses first: the phone is told that answer could not be sent and can retry once earlier answers are confirmed. Other conversations keep working; nothing for you to do unless it keeps happening.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_channel_bytes.wh: How much one conversation's or one view's answers to your phone may have waiting on Cloud at once. It is sized to hold the largest single answer, such as a document, plus the next one behind it, so one busy view cannot hog the line.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_receipts.full: The oldest memories are forgotten early; a late duplicate confirmation then shows up only as an unmatched line in the log. You will not notice anything and do not need to do anything.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_receipts.what: How many recently confirmed answers to your phone this machine remembers for a few minutes, so a repeated confirmation is recognised as a late duplicate rather than something that never existed.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_refusals.full: Past it the extra refusal is dropped and logged, so that phone request gets no answer and waits until it times out after about a minute. Reloading the view later works; nothing else to do.
capacityRow.cloud.spool_refusals.what: How many "could not send this" replies one conversation or view may owe your phone at once. It lets, for example, a whole Board's worth of refused images each get its own reply instead of leaving the phone waiting.
capacityRow.cloud.task_list_reread_secon: A task change is normally sent right away. If one ever slips past the signal, the phone shows it at most this late. Nothing for you to do.

The longest Clawdline goes without re-reading this machine's task list for Cloud when nothing has signaled a change. Re-reading on every pass used to cost hundreds of reads an hour while nothing changed.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_connections.f: A further terminal page is answered busy and does not open until another one closes. Close terminal pages you no longer look at, then try again.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_connections.w: How many terminal views from your phone or other signed-in devices, through Cloud, this machine serves at once. Each one keeps its own encryption key and live screen in memory, so a ceiling stops many open pages from slowing every terminal down.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_ack_se: When time is up the direct connection is ended and the page switches back to the path through Cloud. A key you typed in that moment without a reply is not resent, so check it went in.
How long the machine waits for the phone to confirm it drew a screen sent over a direct connection. Without a confirmation the machine cannot tell whether the phone is still seeing your terminal.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_candid: This is a ceiling on one request. A request listing more is refused as invalid and the terminal stays on the regular path through Cloud; nothing for you to do.

How many possible network addresses one direct-connection request may list for this machine to try. Each one is a network check this machine would make, so a cap stops one request from triggering a flood of them.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_chunk_: When time is up the direct connection is closed and the terminal falls back to the path through Cloud by itself. Nothing for you to do.
How long a large message on a direct terminal connection may stay half-received while its pieces arrive. A message that never finishes should not hold memory or block what comes after it.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_gather: When time is up the machine answers with the addresses it found so far. If those are not enough, the direct connection does not open and the terminal stays on the path through Cloud.
How long this machine spends finding its own network addresses before it answers a direct-connection request. It stops a slow network lookup from keeping the phone waiting.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_messag: This is a ceiling on one message. A larger one closes the direct connection and the terminal falls back to the path through Cloud by itself; nothing for you to do.
How large one message on a direct terminal connection may be once its pieces are put back together. It stops one message from filling this machine's memory.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_negoti: When time is up the attempt is closed and the terminal stays on the regular path through Cloud; it keeps working, just not faster. Nothing for you to do.
How long a direct terminal connection has to actually open after this machine agrees to it. A connection that cannot get through, for example across some networks, should not linger half-open.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_offers: Further attempts in that minute are answered busy and the terminal stays on the regular path through Cloud; the page tries again later by itself. Nothing for you to do.
How often one device may ask, within a minute, to set up a direct connection for a terminal. It also limits how many network checks a stranger's request could make this machine run.
A further device is told busy and simply stays on the regular path through Cloud; its terminal still works, just a little slower. Nothing for you to do.

How many devices may use a direct connection to this machine for terminals, skipping the trip through Cloud so typing feels faster. Each direct connection holds network resources open on this machine.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_probe_: This is a timer, not storage: one check is out at a time. If a check says the device lost access or went offline, its direct connection is closed.

How often the machine checks through Cloud that a device on a direct terminal connection is still allowed in. It is how taking away a device's access also cuts off a direct connection that skips Cloud.
When time is up the direct connection is closed and the page falls back to the path through Cloud, or reconnects. Nothing for you to do.
How long one of those Cloud checks on a direct terminal connection may go unanswered. If Cloud stops answering, a direct connection must not keep running unchecked.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_direct_sdp_by: This is a ceiling on one request. A larger one is refused as invalid and the terminal stays on the regular path through Cloud; nothing for you to do.
How large one request to set up a direct terminal connection may be. It is checked before the request is read, so a malformed or oversized one cannot tie up this machine.
A newer screen simply replaces the held one, so nothing is lost that matters. This lives in each browser tab and the machine cannot count it; nothing for you to do.
How many terminal screens a browser tab holds while it is still waiting to learn which terminal it just opened. Keeping only the newest avoids drawing an outdated screen.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_frame_heartbe: This is a timer, not storage. Each time it passes, the current screen is captured and sent again; you only notice that an idle terminal never shows as stale.

How often the machine resends a terminal screen that has not changed, so the phone knows it is still live. Without it a quiet terminal would look disconnected and the phone would stop sending your keys.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_history_captu: This is a ceiling on one request. Asking for more scrollback than this is refused and the phone gets an error; ask for fewer lines.
How much terminal scrollback the machine reads in one go when the phone asks for it through Cloud. It stops one request from pulling a huge history into memory.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_history_line_: This is a ceiling on one line. If any line in the requested scrollback is longer, that scrollback request is refused and the phone gets an error instead of the lines; the live screen keeps working.
How long a single line of terminal scrollback may be when the phone asks for it through Cloud. One enormous line, such as a minified file printed to the screen, would otherwise fill the whole answer.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_history_recei: This is a ceiling on one answer. When the requested lines do not fit, the newest complete lines are sent and the phone is told how many older lines were left out; nothing for you to do.
How much scrollback one answer to the phone may carry when you scroll up in a terminal through Cloud. Keeping each answer small keeps it moving quickly through Cloud and light on the phone's data.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_ingress.full: Requests beyond it are answered busy and are not carried out; nothing resends them, so a key typed then may need to be typed again.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_ingress.what: How many terminal requests from the phone (keys, pastes, resizes, opening a terminal) may wait for this machine to handle them in order. A short queue keeps a burst from piling up delay behind it.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_key_seconds.f: Before time is up, the phone's page switches to a fresh key by itself without interrupting you. If that switch keeps failing, the old connection closes when its key runs out and the page reconnects.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_key_seconds.w: How long one encryption key for a phone terminal connection lasts. Each key lives only in this machine's memory and the phone's tab, and replacing it regularly limits what a leaked key could ever decrypt.
Further list requests are answered busy; the page tries once more on its own, and if that fails too the list shows an error you can refresh.
How many requests from the phone to list this machine's terminals may wait. Listing has its own short queue, so a slow listing never holds up your typing.
After that one retry, a still-busy list shows an error; wait a moment and refresh. The machine cannot count a page's retries.
How many times a browser page asks again for the list of terminals after Cloud says it is briefly too busy. Typed keys are never retried this way, so nothing is ever typed twice.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_observation_r: The oldest steps are dropped, while the first failures are kept so the start of a problem stays visible. The machine cannot count a page's records; nothing for you to do.
How many recent steps of a terminal connection a browser page records, without any terminal content, so a problem report shows how a disconnect began and where it ended up.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_receipt_busy_: If Cloud still refuses after those tries, that connection is closed and the phone's page reconnects. Nothing for you to do unless it keeps happening.

How many times the machine re-sends a terminal reply after Cloud says your account's terminal traffic allowance for the moment is used up. It turns a brief Cloud slowdown into a delay rather than a dropped connection.
When time is up the reply is sent again; you may see that keystroke's result arrive a moment late. Nothing for you to do.
How long the machine waits before re-sending a terminal reply that Cloud turned away because the account's terminal allowance was spent. Cloud refreshes that allowance every couple of seconds.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_receipt_secon: When time is up the reply is forgotten; by then the phone has stopped waiting and never asks for it again. Nothing for you to do.
How long the machine remembers its reply to each terminal request, so a request that arrives twice is answered again instead of typed twice. It lasts a little past the phone's own wait for a reply.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_receipts.full: The oldest remembered answer is forgotten early so the new keystroke is still answered; you notice nothing, even holding a key down. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_receipts.what: How many recent answers the machine remembers for each phone terminal connection, so a request that arrives twice gets the same answer instead of typing twice. It only bounds memory.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_refusals.full: When even this is full, the extra request gets no answer at all and is only written to the log; the phone gives up on it after a short wait. Nothing to clean up.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_refusals.what: How many busy answers may wait to be sent back when the phone's terminal requests arrive faster than the machine can take them. Turning those away in their own line keeps the phone from waiting in silence.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_request_bytes: This is a ceiling on one request, not something that fills up. A request over it is refused as invalid and nothing is typed; paste a long text in smaller pieces.

The largest single terminal request the phone may send through Cloud, such as typed keys or a paste; the biggest legitimate one is a full-size paste. A cap stops one oversized message from tying up memory before it is even checked.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_revocation_re: When time is up the connection is closed whether or not the notice arrived; the revoked device just loses the terminal. Nothing for you to do.

When you take away a device's terminal access, how long the machine waits for Cloud to confirm that the device was told before it closes the connection anyway. It keeps a revoked device from staying connected.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_roster_deadli: Past it the check counts as failed and access stays closed, not open: terminal input is turned away as busy until a check succeeds. If Cloud stays unreachable, terminals and Session content on the phone stop working until it is back.
How long the machine waits for Cloud to answer that device-list check. Waiting longer would stall typing, and going ahead without the check could let a removed device in.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_roster_refres: When the check is older, the next such action waits for a fresh check or is turned away as busy and retried. You may notice a brief pause; nothing for you to do.

How long a check of your Cloud account's device list is trusted when a phone or browser uses a terminal or reads a Session's content. Keeping it short means a device you remove loses access within seconds.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_roster_retry_: Until the retry, terminal use from Cloud is paused as busy, not revoked, and it resumes once a check succeeds. Nothing for you to do.
After a device-list check fails, how long before the machine tries again. It keeps a Cloud that answers instantly with errors from being asked on every screen update.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_sweep_seconds: This is a timer, not storage. Each pass closes connections that lost access or ran out of time; you only see that a revoked device stops quickly.
How often the machine re-checks every phone terminal connection: whether the device is still allowed, whether any waiting time has run out, and whether a direct connection is still confirmed.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_unconfirmed_s: When time is up without word from the phone, that connection is closed and the phone's page connects again by itself. Nothing for you to do.

After the phone opens a terminal connection or switches it to a new key, how long the machine waits for the phone to show it received the reply. A connection the phone never picked up should not hold a slot.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_unverified_re: The connection is then closed without treating the device as removed; that screen stops updating and has to connect again to continue.

How long a phone or browser's terminal connection is kept paused while the machine cannot confirm that device is still allowed. Pausing guards against a removed device; the time limit bounds how long a dead connection is held open.
capacityRow.cloud.terminal_viewer_connec: Another connection from the same device is answered busy. The device's page normally switches over and releases the old one by itself; if a terminal stays stuck as busy, close the extra terminal tabs on that device.
How many terminal connections one signed-in device may hold to this machine through Cloud: one in use, plus one while it switches to a fresh key. It keeps one device from taking every terminal slot.
capacityRow.cloud.viewer_events_batch_by: This is a ceiling on one batch. A larger batch is refused; the page drops and counts it, then sends the reports after it. You see nothing and need not act.
How big one batch of error reports from the Cloud web page or phone may be. The page sends its own failures here so a problem seen on the phone shows up in this machine's log.
capacityRow.cloud.viewer_events_line_byt: This is a ceiling on one line. A longer report is cut and the line says it was cut. Nothing for you to do.
How long one error report from the Cloud page may be once written as a line in this machine's log, so one report cannot bloat the log.
capacityRow.cloud.viewer_events_logged_r: The rest of that batch is written as one count on the batch's summary line instead of one line each. Nothing for you to do.
How many error reports from one batch sent by the Cloud page each get their own line in this machine's log, so a misbehaving page cannot flood the log in one go.
capacityRow.cloud.viewer_events_seen_bat: The oldest remembered batch is forgotten first; if that one is resent later, it is written again, so at worst a report appears twice and none is lost. Nothing for you to do.
How many recent batches of error reports from the Cloud page Clawdline remembers, so a batch the page resends after losing the reply is not written into the log twice.
An earlier offer blocks another until the interval ends. New traffic may then request one fresh exchange; no timer retries it. Disconnect discards pending secrets. The machine cannot measure this browser interval.
The minimum seconds between content-key offers from one browser client, shared across its machines. This bounds retries caused by unknown-key traffic.
capacityRow.cloud.viewer_rekey_pending.f: Further unknown-key envelopes retain no payload and start no extra operation. One exchange expires within 120 seconds; it is never automatically retried. This feature is disabled by default. The machine cannot measure live browser use.
capacityRow.cloud.viewer_rekey_pending.w: How many content-key exchanges one browser client may hold at once. Only an explicitly paired machine can answer; read-only browsers are eligible.
capacityRow.console.next_messages.what: Shares this browser’s existing pending-card budget with next-message inputs.
capacityRow.console.next_messages.full: New queued input is refused; the editor and existing queued messages stay intact.
capacityRow.console.assistant_facts_read: After 15 seconds the request is canceled and capability-dependent actions remain unavailable. Late answers cannot authorize another machine or execution.
Limits how long a mounted view waits for the selected machine’s assistant capabilities.
capacityRow.console.carrier_receive_byte: When the budget is full, the affected direct connection closes and its reads use the existing fallback policy. The daemon cannot measure another browser’s queue.
Encoded direct-connection replies waiting for authentication in this browser. The 32 MiB budget is shared across its machines.
capacityRow.console.carrier_receive_rows: At 32 pending replies, the affected direct connection closes instead of retaining an unbounded queue. The daemon cannot measure another browser’s pending replies.
Direct-connection replies waiting for authentication in this browser. Wire order is preserved so slower decryption cannot be mistaken for replay.
capacityRow.console.direct_history_hours: Older hours are dropped. Nothing is lost that you need: Sessions keep working through the Cloud relay either way.
How many hours of direct-connection attempts this browser remembers for each machine. The machine sheet draws them so you can see when the direct path stopped opening.
capacityRow.console.direct_history_machi: Past it, the record of the machine you have not used for the longest is dropped. Its next attempt starts a new record.
How many machines this browser keeps a direct-connection record for.
capacityRow.console.execution_recovery_a: If recovery fails or the Session changes again, the page keeps the failure and offers manual recovery. Messages and other actions are never resent automatically.
Automatic recovery attempts when an opened Session is no longer current. One attempt per opening keeps a changing Session from causing repeated reloads.
Each time it passes the light checks again, which is also when a new version or a signed-out browser is noticed. Nothing for you to do.

How often the connection light checks the daemon while this machine's live updates are flowing. The open stream already proves the daemon is up, so checking every 15 seconds was wasted requests; a dropped stream or a Cloud page keeps the 15-second check.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_body_bytes: A larger answer is refused unread and that read says so.
The largest Cloud answer the connection-health page accepts.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_budget_sec: Reads still running when it runs out are marked as out of time rather than left blank.
How long one load of the connection-health page may take, every read included.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_event_page: At the bound, loading older records is replaced by a note to narrow the window.
How many pages of records the connection-health page keeps at once.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_export_byt: A larger record is not copied, and the page says how large it would be.
The largest evidence record the connection-health page copies.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_id_charact: A longer id names no screen, so the page says the address is unknown.
The longest trace or boot id an operator address may carry.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_incident_e: A larger export stops being read, and nothing is kept or offered.
The largest incident export the connection-health page keeps for download or copy.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_incident_p: Older incidents are not loaded, and the page says to pause at an earlier time.
The pages of the incident list the connection-health page holds at once.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_incident_r: More incidents are not shown, and the page says more were opened in that window.
The incidents the connection-health page asks Cloud for in one list.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_incident_w: How far back the connection-health page lists incidents by when they opened.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_investigat: An oversized reference list is refused rather than silently omitting evidence.
The stored evidence references accepted in one investigation report.
An oversized list is refused; an unreadable response is not shown as no investigations.
The investigations accepted for one incident in this page.
A longer list than Cloud's own bound is refused, not cut short.
How many records the connection-health page asks for per page.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_parallel_r: Further reads wait their turn instead of being refused by Cloud as busy.
How many connection-health reads one page runs at once, matching what Cloud admits per operator.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_probe_clai: A longer claim list is refused so an unsupported claim cannot be silently hidden.
The evidence and limitation statements accepted in each probe claim list.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_probe_host: The page refuses an oversized host list and cannot claim complete probe coverage.
The registered and retained probe hosts one response may describe.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_probe_targ: The page refuses an oversized response instead of silently omitting target results.
The target results an independent-probe response may contain.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_reads_per_: Each screen asks for a fixed set; it never reads once per row.
How many Cloud reads one connection-health screen asks for per load.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_refresh_se: Between reads the page can be this far behind; pausing stops the reads.
How often a live connection-health page reads Cloud again.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_request_se: That read shows as timed out in its own panel; the reads that answered stay on screen.
How long the connection-health page waits for one Cloud read before marking it timed out.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_trend_lane: More sources are listed in the table only, and the page says how many are drawn.
The sources the connection-health trend view draws as charts.
capacityRow.console.health_ui_trend_sign: Older buckets are counted, not listed.
The trend buckets the connection-health page lists to investigate.
capacityRow.console.machine_list_poll_se: Between checks the list can be a few seconds behind. Closing and reopening the page reads it again right away.
How often the open machine list checks each machine again, so whether reads go direct or through Cloud stays current.
capacityRow.console.native_pairing_save_: After that long the app stops waiting, shows no code, and lets you try saving again or ignore the request. If this keeps happening, restart Clawdline and pair again.

When a phone or browser asks to pair, how long the desktop app waits for the service to save the permission you chose before the six-digit code is shown. Without it, a stalled service would hold the pairing until the code expires.
capacityRow.console.opened_row_quiet_sec: The pane then says the machine has not sent this Session instead of saying it is reading. If it stays that way, check that the machine is online and Clawdline is running there.
How long the page waits for the Session you opened to arrive from your machine before it stops saying it is still reading. This keeps a blank pane from claiming to be loading forever.
capacityRow.console.opened_row_restate_s: If the Session is still missing, the page asks again after this interval; it usually appears within a second. Nothing for you to do.

On Cloud, when the Session you opened is missing from the page's list, the page asks your machine to send its list again, at most this often. Without asking, an idle Session took about 20 seconds to appear; the ceiling keeps the page from flooding the machine with asks.
capacityRow.console.owner_retention_poll: A read still out when the next one is due is not doubled: that tick is skipped.
How often an open Settings window reads the owner-diagnostics switch and its sender's status again.
capacityRow.console.owner_retention_requ: Past it the read is abandoned and the block says the status is unknown instead of repeating the last answer.
How long one read of the owner-diagnostics switch and sender status may take.
capacityRow.console.persona_retry_second: The page retries automatically and restores role names when the machine answers. If the machine remains offline, roles return after it reconnects.

How long the page waits before retrying a role catalog read that failed because the machine connection or server was temporarily unavailable. During the gap, Session roles may be missing from the list.
capacityRow.console.pinned_list_read_tim: After that much silence the page stops waiting on that request and falls back to other ways of getting the list, so it may arrive late. If this keeps happening, check the machine's network.

On Cloud, how long the page waits for your machine to answer a request for its Session list before giving up on that attempt. Without it, a stalled connection would leave the list waiting with no end.
capacityRow.console.relay_feature_wait_s: After the wait the read is sent to the machine anyway and the machine's own answer decides; at worst the first read on a page is a few seconds slower. Nothing for you to do.

When a Cloud page has just opened, how long a read waits to learn which actions your machine supports. An old remembered list could wrongly claim the machine cannot read a conversation, so waiting avoids a false "not supported" error.
capacityRow.console.relay_transcript_exp: Past this age the page's previous answer counts as old and the machine is asked again; at worst a new reply shows a few seconds later. Nothing for you to do.

Over Cloud, for a short while after you send something, the page asks your machine for the conversation again at most this often unless the conversation shows new activity. Each ask travels through Cloud to the machine, so this stops a phone from sending one every two seconds.
capacityRow.console.session_notes_safety: When it passes the page reads them again, so a to-do changed elsewhere can take up to this long to show. Nothing for you to do.

How often, at most, an open Session page rereads its to-dos, and its attention notes while that panel is open, besides rereading when you come back to the page. It catches changes the live updates missed without checking constantly.
capacityRow.console.status_gap_retry_sec: The page retries by itself and the missing Session usually appears on the next try. If it never does, check the machine's connection.

On Cloud, when one Session is missing from the list and fetching it again was refused or timed out, how long the page waits before trying again. This keeps one failed attempt from leaving the list marked incomplete for the rest of the update.
capacityRow.console.status_marker_recove: After the wait the page stops waiting for the stored copy and asks the machine for its list directly; the list may show a few seconds later. Nothing for you to do.
