capacityRow.terminal.launch_line_bytes.w: The longest command line Clawdline types straight into a new iTerm2 tab or tmux pane to start an assistant. macOS cuts a longer line short at that moment, and the assistant would never start.
capacityRow.terminal.launch_scripts.full: The oldest leftover scripts are removed first when a new one is written. Nothing visible happens and there is nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.terminal.launch_scripts.what: How many of those small launch scripts, written for commands too long to type into a new tab, may be kept at once. Each deletes itself when its tab runs it, but one a tab never ran would otherwise pile up on disk.
capacityRow.terminal.lease_seconds.full: If it lapses, your next keystrokes are refused with a message that your control lapsed, anything not yet confirmed is dropped, and anyone may take control. Take control again to keep typing.
capacityRow.terminal.lease_seconds.what: How long your control of a terminal lasts without being renewed; only the holder can type. The page renews it automatically while open, so a closed or lost tab does not lock everyone else out.
capacityRow.terminal.paste_bytes.full: A bigger paste is refused and nothing is typed; the page says it was too much input. Paste it in smaller pieces.
capacityRow.terminal.paste_bytes.what: How large one paste into a terminal may be. A huge paste would tie up the terminal and the program receiving it for a long time.
capacityRow.terminal.streams.full: Another viewer is refused; the message currently says the terminal has too many viewers even when it is this machine-wide limit that was reached. Close terminal tabs you are not using and try again.
capacityRow.terminal.streams.what: How many live terminal screen streams the machine serves at once, across all terminals and viewers. Each stream sends screen updates continuously, so this bounds how much work terminals can give the machine.
capacityRow.terminal.viewers.full: Another viewer is refused with a message that the terminal has too many viewers; nobody already watching is cut off. Close a tab that has this terminal open and try again.
capacityRow.terminal.viewers.what: How many browser tabs or phones can watch one terminal at the same time. Each viewer gets its own continuous stream of screen updates from the machine.
capacityRow.update.apply_body_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one request, not something that fills. A request over it is refused as malformed and no update starts; the update button never sends one that large.
capacityRow.update.apply_body_bytes.what: How large one request to start an update may be. A real request only names a version and a couple of options, so anything longer is not a real request.
capacityRow.update.build_body_bytes.full: A larger answer is refused as not being a version file; the update status shows an error and keeps the last good answer. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.update.build_body_bytes.what: How large the small version file Clawdline reads may be, from app.clawdline.com or from its own web files, when comparing a source build with the hosted console. The real file is tiny, so anything bigger is not it.
capacityRow.update.fetch_timeout_seconds: When time is up the check is abandoned; the update status keeps the last good answer and shows the error beside it. It tries again later by itself.
On a machine running a build from source, how long one check of the version app.clawdline.com serves may take. A slow network should not leave the check hanging.
capacityRow.update.refresh_seconds.full: When time is up it simply checks again in the background; until then the update status shows the last answer. Installed releases don't use this. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.update.refresh_seconds.what: On a machine running a build from source, how often Clawdline re-checks which version app.clawdline.com is serving, to tell you whether this machine is behind. Checking now and then avoids asking the network on every page load.
capacityRow.usage.daily_days.full: Older daily summaries expire. Missing history remains a gap; cumulative Session totals stay available.
capacityRow.usage.daily_days.what: The local calendar days retained for each transcript in the usage overview. This covers two adjacent 28-day periods and today.
capacityRow.usage.daily_rows.full: The oldest summaries are removed. The overview reports partial, truncated history instead of treating missing days as zero.
capacityRow.usage.daily_rows.what: The daily token summaries retained across all transcript sources. The ceiling bounds the storage used by the overview.
capacityRow.usage.overview_tasks.full: Only the newest tasks in the requested period are included, and coverage says the result is truncated. No task records are deleted.
capacityRow.usage.overview_tasks.what: The dispatched tasks read by one usage overview request to calculate counts and successful elapsed-time samples.
capacityRow.usage.work_cursor_queue.full: Further moments are not measured; they are marked as missing, and the cost report shows that piece of work's cost as unknown rather than zero. Your work itself is not affected. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.usage.work_cursor_queue.what: How many start-or-end moments of work are waiting to have their token usage snapshotted. Snapshots are taken in the background so dispatching and Board changes never wait on them; the queue keeps a backlog from eating memory.
capacityRow.usage.work_cursor_rows.full: The oldest snapshots are deleted as new ones arrive, so the cost breakdown of very old work can no longer be computed. Each Session's total usage is kept elsewhere and stays intact. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.usage.work_cursor_rows.what: How many token-usage snapshots Clawdline keeps to work out what one piece of work cost (a child task, a Board item, one of its steps). Each start and end leaves a snapshot, so without a ceiling the record would grow with every task forever.
This is a ceiling on one report, not storage that fills up. Older work is left out and the report says it was cut short; ask for a later start date to see more. Nothing is deleted.
How many pieces of work one per-work cost report lists, newest first. A ceiling keeps one report from reading through months of history and taking a long time to answer.
capacityRow.voice.model_download_bytes.f: A response larger than the pinned model is refused and its partial file is removed. The previously installed model, if any, stays untouched; try again after checking the network or upstream source.
capacityRow.voice.model_download_bytes.w: How much of the pinned speech model Clawdline will accept while downloading it. The ceiling is the model's exact upstream size, so an error page or an unexpectedly larger response cannot fill the disk or become a usable model.
capacityRow.waits.open.full: A Session asking to hold or wait on more files is refused and told so; open holds are never dropped. They clear when their owners release them or the waiters leave.
capacityRow.waits.open.what: How many file holds are open at once: a Session holding some files while others wait for it to let go, so two Sessions do not edit the same files together.
capacityRow.work.assignments.full: Assigning another item to a new Session is refused until pending ones finish opening or fail. Answer or close the new Sessions that are waiting.
capacityRow.work.assignments.what: How many Board assignments to a new Session are still being set up: recorded, but the new Session has not opened or is waiting for its first screen to be answered.
capacityRow.work.completion_reason_bytes: This is a ceiling on one note. A longer one is refused with a message that it is too long, and the item is not changed; shorten it and try again.
How long the note may be when you mark a Board item done yourself, or when a Session explains why a completion must be taken back. It is a reason, kept in the item's history, not a place for logs.
capacityRow.work.digests.full: When a new digest is written the oldest one is deleted. The facts it summarised stay in the Board's own history; nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.work.digests.what: How many daily and weekly digests of the Board are kept, about two years' worth. Each is a summary of what moved, so keeping them forever would only grow the data file.
capacityRow.work.documents_per_item.full: Adding a new document is refused. Revising an existing one with the same title still works, and a completion report is always accepted.
capacityRow.work.documents_per_item.what: How many documents (spec, design, test notes and the like) one Board item may hold, so one item cannot grow into an unreadable pile.
capacityRow.work.image_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one image. One still too large after resizing is refused and not saved. Try a smaller or simpler image.
capacityRow.work.image_bytes.what: How big one reference image on a Board item may be after Clawdline resizes and re-encodes it.
capacityRow.work.image_bytes_per_item.fu: Adding another image to that item is refused and nothing is removed. Remove one of its images first, or use a smaller one.
capacityRow.work.image_bytes_per_item.wh: The total size of all reference images on one Board item, so one item cannot hold most of the image space.
capacityRow.work.image_bytes_total.full: Adding any new reference image is refused and nothing is removed. Delete items or images you no longer need to make room.
capacityRow.work.image_bytes_total.what: The total size of all reference images on Board items and Session to-dos, so pictures cannot quietly fill this machine's disk.
capacityRow.work.image_request_body_byte: This is a ceiling on one upload. A larger one is refused before anything is saved. Pick a smaller file.
How large one image upload to a Board item or to-do may be as it arrives, from this computer or the phone, before Clawdline even looks at the picture.
capacityRow.work.images_per_item.full: Adding another image is refused with a message that the item already has its images. Remove one first if you need to add another.
capacityRow.work.images_per_item.what: How many reference images one Board item may hold, so its page stays quick to open on the phone.
This is a ceiling on one text. A longer one is refused when saved, and the command line refuses it before sending; split the material into a document or shorten it.

How long a Board item's description may be; the same ceiling applies to its acceptance criteria and to one attached document. Every Session working the item reads this text, so a huge one makes every turn slow and expensive.
capacityRow.work.item_title_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one title. A longer one is refused when saved and you are asked to shorten it; titles taken from a pasted list are cut off with an ellipsis instead.
capacityRow.work.item_title_bytes.what: How long a Board item's title may be; the same ceiling applies to a step's title and a reference image's title. Titles appear in lists, cards and phone notifications, so they need to fit on a line or two.
This is a ceiling on one note. Saving a longer one is refused and it must be shortened; nothing already on the item changes.
How long the note on a Board item telling you what you need to do may be. It is meant to be one clear request you can act on, not a report.
capacityRow.work.list_page_rows.full: This is a ceiling on one page, not on your items. The rest stay saved and load on the next page. Nothing for you to do.
capacityRow.work.list_page_rows.what: How many Board items load on the first page, so the Board appears quickly instead of waiting for every item and its documents and images.
capacityRow.work.open.full: Creating a new item is refused. Close or drop items you no longer need in the Board or Backlog to make room.
capacityRow.work.open.what: How many open items you have on the Board and in the Backlog. Each is someone's plan or commitment, so Clawdline never removes one to make room.
capacityRow.work.planning.full: Creating a new Plan is refused. Finish or cancel Plans you no longer need to make room.
capacityRow.work.planning.what: How many open Plan items (saved plans or investigation directions) you keep. Each is your own plan, so none is removed to make room.
capacityRow.work.request_body_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one request. A larger one is refused with a message that it is too large and nothing is saved; shorten the text or move long material into a document.
capacityRow.work.request_body_bytes.what: How large one change to the Board may be when sent from the console, the phone through Cloud, or the command line. It stops one oversized request from tying up the daemon or a phone's data.
The Session is told it cannot record another landing for this item, and every earlier record stays. Reaching it means the item has been reopened many times; put further work in a new item.

How many times one Board item can record that its Session landed a commit on a target branch and its remote. Each record is proof kept forever, so a ceiling stops an item reopened over and over from piling up proof without end.
capacityRow.work.steps_per_item.full: Adding another subtask is refused. Split the work into separate Board items instead.
capacityRow.work.steps_per_item.what: How many subtasks one Board item may list, so a single item stays readable and does not quietly become a whole project.
capacityRow.work_gate_claims_per_round.f: A verdict with more claims is refused whole and none of it is kept, which counts as a technical failure of the check. Keep acceptance criteria to a reviewable number of points.
capacityRow.work_gate_claims_per_round.w: How many separate claims one checker's verdict may contain, each one an acceptance point it judged. A ceiling keeps one verdict small enough to store and review.
The rest stay queued and are picked up in the next pass, so a busy moment only delays a check a little. Nothing is dropped and there is nothing for you to do.

How many waiting verification jobs (checks to start, results to pass on, cleanups) Clawdline handles in one background pass. Doing them in small batches keeps one pass from holding up everything else.
capacityRow.work_gate_evidence_artifact_: This is a ceiling on one file. A larger file is refused before it is stored, both by the command and by Clawdline; the checker must trim it or attach an excerpt.
How large one evidence file a checker attaches may be. A screenshot or log excerpt fits easily; a whole video or build output would fill the disk with one check.
capacityRow.work_gate_evidence_artifacts: This is a ceiling on one checker. Another file is refused before anything is written, and the files already attached stay; the checker must choose which evidence matters.
How many evidence files (screenshots, logs, recordings) one checker may attach while verifying a Board item. Each is kept on disk with the item, so a ceiling stops one check from filling it.
capacityRow.work_gate_evidence_string_by: This is a ceiling on one piece of evidence. A verdict with a longer one is refused whole and the checker must shorten it; longer material belongs in an attached evidence file.
How long one piece of written evidence in a checker's verdict may be. Evidence should point at something specific, such as a file and line or a command's result, not paste whole outputs.
capacityRow.work_gate_evidence_strings_p: This is a ceiling on one claim. A verdict that cites more is refused whole and the checker must submit a tighter one; nothing partial is kept.
How many pieces of written evidence a checker may cite for one claim in its verdict. A few concrete pieces are what you need to trust a claim; dozens would hide them.
capacityRow.work_gate_evidence_total_byt: This is a ceiling on one checker. A file that would go over is refused before it is stored; what is already attached stays.
How much evidence, all files together, one checker may attach while verifying a Board item. It caps the disk one check can use even when each file is within its own ceiling.
capacityRow.work_gate_owner_offline_grac: When time is up the decision passes to you: the item shows it is waiting for you, and you get one notification. Decide on the item.

How long Clawdline waits for an Epic's owner Session to come back online when a child item's verification needs its decision. A short absence shouldn't pull you in, but a stalled decision shouldn't wait forever.
capacityRow.work_gate_recent_rounds_per_: Older rounds are not shown in detail but stay stored, and the item still shows the totals and the latest result, with a note that the list was cut short. Nothing for you to do.
How many recent verification rounds are shown in detail when you open one Board item. Showing the latest few keeps the item quick to open, especially on the phone.
capacityRow.work_gate_result_bytes.full: This is a ceiling on one verdict. A larger one is refused before anything is saved, and the checker must send a smaller one.
capacityRow.work_gate_result_bytes.what: How large one checker's whole verdict may be. The verdict is stored with the Board item and decides whether work may merge, so it has to stay a reviewable size.
capacityRow.work_gate_retry_backoff_seco: When the wait is over the check is tried again on its own. You might see verification start a few minutes late; there is nothing for you to do.

How long Clawdline waits before trying again to start a checker that could not start because Clawdline was too busy, or whose start was not confirmed. Waiting avoids hammering a busy machine, and the cap stops it waiting indefinitely.
capacityRow.work_gate_round_details_per_: A new verification round for this item is refused, so it cannot pass verification. In the item's verification panel, export the closed rounds, save the file, then confirm the purge.

How many independent verification rounds one Board item keeps in full detail (each time a checker examines the work before it can merge). This is evidence, so it is never deleted on its own; the ceiling stops one item from holding it without end.
No item can start a new verification round until space is made. Open items with many old rounds, export their closed rounds in the verification panel, save the file and confirm the purge.
How many independent verification rounds Clawdline keeps in full detail across all Board items. Each round's evidence stays until you clear it, so this keeps the total from filling the database.
capacityRow.work_gate_tasks_per_round.fu: A third start is refused and the round is escalated as a technical problem on the Board item, where a decision is needed: repair and retry, override, or cancel.
capacityRow.work_gate_tasks_per_round.wh: How many times one verification round may start a checker: the first try plus one retry after a technical failure. Endless retries would burn time and tokens on something that keeps breaking.
clawdfatherMenu.limitReached: Clawdfather already holds every action this machine keeps. Delete one before adding another.
clawdfatherMenu.name: Name
count.prunedInterventions: Older handled notes cleaned up locally: {arg0}.
count.skillFoldersSkipped: Skill folders skipped because they could not be read safely: {arg0}. Check their links or permissions on the machine.
dispatchPolicy.baseIntro: Clawdline supplies these rules. Your additions above are kept separately.
dispatchPolicy.changed: The rules changed elsewhere. Copy your draft before reloading.
dispatchPolicy.failed: Could not read or save the dispatch rules.
dispatchPolicy.intro: These additions guide work handed to another Session. They are read at each dispatch.
dispatchPolicy.legacy: Showing rules carried over from the retired app. Saving moves them into this version.
dispatchPolicy.saved: Saved. The next dispatch uses these rules.
dispatchPolicy.title: My dispatch rules
documents.connectingDetail: It opens by itself once connected; there is no need to reload.

documents.empty: No documents or MP4 videos are available to show for this Session.
documents.readFailed: The document could not be read.
documents.shareUnavailable: A Cloud share link could not be created. Check this document's host identity.
documents.shareUnavailableError: This browser cannot share or copy the document link.
documents.videoChanged: The video changed. Open it again.
documents.videoError: This browser cannot play this video. Use an MP4 with H.264/AAC encoding.
documents.videoNotFound: This published video could not be found.
documents.videoReadFailed: The video could not be read. Try again.
documents.videoTooLarge: The video exceeds 32 MiB. Export a smaller MP4.

health.at_failed: What is waiting for you could not be read ({code}). This is not the same as nothing waiting.
health.at_incomplete: Cloud could not check everything; more may be waiting than is listed here.
health.at_loading: Reading what is waiting for you…
health.at_noneIncomplete: Nothing was listed, but Cloud could not check everything, so something may still be waiting.
health.at_reason_fix_prepared: The Agent that investigated this incident prepared a fix, but Cloud has not confirmed that the incident recovered. Review the fix before relying on it.
health.at_reason_no_investigation: Cloud opened this incident and no Agent has investigated it yet. Starting an investigation is your decision.
health.at_reason_unknown: Cloud listed this incident for a reason this console does not recognise yet. Open the incident to see what Cloud recorded.
health.at_reason_verification_failed: The Agent that investigated this incident reported that verification failed. This does not say the incident is resolved; review the result and decide the next step.
health.at_reason_verified_recovered: Cloud verified that this incident recovered after an Agent's investigation. Cloud does not close the incident by itself; review the result and acknowledge it if you agree.
health.at_unavailable: Cloud cannot list what is waiting for you right now. This is not the same as nothing waiting.
health.basis_ordering: From ordering only; nothing shows why
health.copyFailed: This browser refused the clipboard. The text is selected; press ⌘C or Ctrl+C.
health.evidenceExampleNote: Built from example data, not from captured diagnostics.
health.evidenceLead: Built from the snapshot this scope was authorized to read. Forbidden items keep only their source.
health.evidenceTooLarge: The record is larger than {kb} KiB and was not built.
health.failedBody: No health is shown, because none could be confirmed. This is not a healthy result.
health.failedTitle: Connection health could not be loaded
health.failure_contract_bound: The service answered with more rows than this page shows.
health.failure_contract_schema: The service answered with a schema this page does not read.
health.failure_contract_shape: The service answered with a malformed record.
health.failure_forbidden: This account may not read this scope.
health.failure_http_error: The health service refused the request.
health.failure_network: The health service could not be reached.
health.failure_rate_limited: Too many requests. The next refresh will try again.
health.failure_timeout: The health service did not answer within 5 seconds.
health.failure_unauthorized: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
health.failure_unsupported: This service does not provide connection health yet.
health.flt_allLoaded: All {n} records of this window are loaded ({pages} pages).
health.flt_allLoadedFiltered: All {n} records matching this filter in this window are loaded ({pages} pages). Cloud filtered them.
health.flt_more: {n} records loaded in {pages} pages; the window holds more. Pause to load older pages.
health.flt_moreFiltered: {n} matching records loaded in {pages} pages; Cloud holds more matching ones in this window. Pause to load older pages.
health.hiddenCount: {n} items are not visible in this scope.
health.inc_ackConfirmObserved: This writes revision {n}, closing the incident by your review. Recovery was observed; the evidence stays exactly as it is.
health.inc_ackConfirmUnobserved: This writes revision {n}, closing the incident by your review. No recovery was observed, and closing does not say it recovered. New evidence reopens it.
health.inc_ackMeaning: Acknowledgement is a person's review, recorded as a new revision. It never marks recovery and nothing acknowledges automatically.
health.inc_ackNoChange: Already closed over the same evidence; no revision was written.
health.inc_acked: Acknowledged. The closing revision is loading.
health.inc_buildsNote: Builds are as each producer declared them; Cloud does not verify them.
health.inc_card_measured: Operation duration reported by the source
health.inc_closedNote: Closed means a person reviewed the incident. It is not a health verdict.
health.inc_contextNote: Neighbouring records from the same producer, frozen with the incident for context.
health.inc_disabled: Incidents are turned off in Cloud. None are being opened, so an empty list does not mean nothing happened.
health.inc_evidenceNote: Each card is one frozen record, explained in words. The exact fields are under Technical record.
health.inc_evt_other: A record of another kind; its exact name is under Technical record.
health.inc_evt_recovered: Recovery: the producer recorded the operation moving on.
health.inc_evt_released_after_stall: Released after a stall: the operation moved on, but whether it succeeded was not recorded.
health.inc_evt_scheduling_gap: The producer's own scheduling fell behind.
health.inc_evt_slow_detected: Slow signal: the producer's watchdog saw the operation stay at one stage past its slow threshold. An observation at that moment, not a final result.
health.inc_evt_stall_detected: Stall signal: the producer's watchdog saw no progress past its stall threshold. An observation at that moment; it does not say the operation never finished.
health.inc_evt_state_after_loss: The watchdog's state right after that loss.
health.inc_evt_transitions_lost: The producer reported that it lost some monitoring records.
health.inc_exp_export_too_large: The export was larger than 1 MiB, Cloud's own bound, so it was not kept.
health.inc_exp_hash_mismatch: The bundle did not match its content hash, so nothing was kept.
health.inc_exp_not_json: The export was not readable JSON, so nothing was kept.
health.inc_exp_wrong_incident: Cloud returned a different incident or revision, so nothing was kept.
health.inc_expiredBody: The incident's frozen evidence passed retention and is no longer kept. Nothing from before is shown.
health.inc_exportNote: Cloud's own audited export of this revision. Its hash is checked here before you can download or copy it.
health.inc_head_loss: {source} reported that it lost monitoring records, so part of what it did is not known.
health.inc_head_slow: {source} reported a slow operation: it stayed at one stage longer than the producer's own slow threshold.
health.inc_head_stall: {source} reported a stall: an operation made no progress at one stage for longer than the producer's own stall threshold.
health.inc_held: {n} incidents held from {pages} pages; older ones opened in this window are not loaded.
health.inc_heldAll: All {n} incidents opened in this window are loaded ({pages} pages).
health.inc_miss_gaps: Sequence numbers are missing ({ranges}): those records never reached Cloud.
health.inc_miss_lost: The producer reported {n} monitoring transitions it could not record.
health.inc_miss_noEnd: No record shows the operation reaching its final response or recovering.
health.inc_miss_noEndAfter: No final response was recorded after this stage.
health.inc_miss_none: Nothing is listed as missing in this revision.
health.inc_miss_overflow: The producer reported {n} records dropped because its buffer was full.
health.inc_miss_refused: {n} records were not frozen into this incident because it reached its size bound.
health.inc_miss_unverified: The producer's sequence could not be verified, so records may be missing without a visible gap.
health.inc_moreRows: Showing the newest {n}; more incidents opened in this window.
health.inc_next_export: To hand this to an engineer or an agent, export this revision at the end of the page; it carries every raw field.
health.inc_next_logs: Search the service's own logs around {last} for the request at this stage; these records do not name the request's route.
health.inc_next_machine: Open the machine page to see this producer's other records around that time.
health.inc_next_monitoring: Open monitoring status to see whether this producer was losing records at that time.
health.inc_next_review: Read the recovery record below; if it is enough, acknowledge the incident.
health.inc_next_trace: Open the request trace for this operation: it shows every record Cloud still holds for it, including any received after this revision.
health.inc_noAggregates: Trends wider than these incidents are not collected.
health.inc_noHypotheses: No hypotheses: Cloud does not derive any, and none are made up here.
health.inc_noPrevious: None: this is the first revision
health.inc_noTimeRule: States never change with time: silence is not recovery.
health.inc_none: No incident opened in this window. Refused incidents are counted above.
health.inc_noneDisabled: No incidents: Cloud is not opening them.
health.inc_noneForTrace: No incident on the page held names this operation.
health.inc_noneOpenNote: None open on the first page; this is not a health verdict.
health.inc_now_active: No ending and no recovery were recorded after these signals. Whether the operation is still stuck now is unknown: this revision only shows that no later record about it was frozen here.
health.inc_now_age: The newest record here is {age} older than this read ({asOf}); both times are Cloud's clock.
health.inc_now_closed: A person reviewed and closed this incident. Closed is not a health verdict.
health.inc_now_limits: These records do not establish the cause, or what happened to the operation after {last}.
health.inc_now_limitsNoTime: These records do not establish the cause, or what happened to the operation afterwards.
health.inc_now_recovered: A recovery record was received at {time}. A person has not reviewed it yet.
health.inc_now_recovering: A later record arrived, but it does not prove recovery.
health.inc_older: You are viewing revision {n} of {of}. It is immutable and may be out of date.
health.inc_olderFailed: Older incidents could not be loaded: {reason}. The incidents above are unchanged.
health.inc_out_pendingNote: Pending means the stage had not ended when this record was written. It is not a final result and says nothing about now.
health.inc_pageBound: This page holds at most {n} incidents. Pause at an earlier time to see older ones.
health.inc_pauseToPage: Pause to load older incidents: the list pages over one fixed window.
health.inc_problemLine: {n} open incidents on the first page.
health.inc_recoveryObserved: Recovery observed with exact sequence coverage.
health.inc_refused: {n} incidents were refused at a bound ({reasons}); an absent incident may be one of them.
health.inc_stg_account_dispatch_returned: the account's storage object had answered the worker
health.inc_stg_account_dispatch_started: the worker had passed the request to the account's storage object and was waiting for it
health.inc_stg_account_pinned: the request had been tied to its account
health.inc_stg_api_admitted: the API had accepted the request
health.inc_stg_api_dependency_completed: the downstream call had returned to the API; this stage alone does not show a final response
health.inc_stg_api_dependency_started: the API had called a downstream dependency and was waiting for it
health.inc_stg_api_handler_completed: the API's handler had finished its own work
health.inc_stg_api_response_completed: the API had sent its final response
health.inc_stg_do_entered: the request had entered the account's storage object
health.inc_stg_do_handler_returned: the storage object's handler had returned
health.inc_stg_do_runtime_ready: the storage object was ready to run the request
health.inc_stg_fanout_sent: a message had been handed to a socket, which does not prove anyone received it
health.inc_stg_other: a stage this page has no description for
health.inc_stg_outer_settled: the worker had finished the request
health.inc_stg_storage_completed: the storage read or write had returned
health.inc_stg_storage_started: the storage object had started a storage read or write and was waiting for it
health.inc_stg_worker_admitted: the Cloud worker had accepted the request
health.inc_sum_noStage: The records do not say which stage the operation was at.
health.inc_sum_nowTitle: What this evidence can and cannot say now
health.inc_sum_waited: The source reported an operation duration of {time}. This does not measure time spent at this stage.
health.inc_sum_when: Cloud received the first record at {first} and the last record of this revision at {last}.
health.inc_techNote: Revision hashes, sizes, retention, the manifest and raw stage names. The summary above is derived from these same fields.
health.inc_techTitle: Technical details for engineers and agents
health.inc_why_not_recovery_evidence: The newest record is not recovery evidence.
health.inc_why_released_outcome_unknown: Released after the stall; whether it succeeded is unknown.
health.inc_why_sequence_gap: Records are missing between the problem and the recovery, so recovery is not proven.
health.inc_why_sequence_unverified: The sequence between the problem and the recovery could not be verified.
health.incidentNotFound: This incident is not in the loaded window.
health.incidentsNone: No incident was opened in this window.
health.iv_ambiguous: No answer reached this page, so it may already have started. Sending again repeats the same request and cannot start a second one.
health.iv_bindConfirm: This webhook is bound to an investigation schedule on its machine.
health.iv_bindNote: Choose the machine that runs it. Only a machine Cloud has confirmed has one investigation schedule can be chosen; every other machine says what it needs.
health.iv_destFailed: Your machines could not be read: {reason}
health.iv_destIncomplete: This list may be incomplete: Cloud left some machines out, or sent a state this page does not know.
health.iv_destNext_ambiguous: Keep one investigation schedule bound on this machine and unbind the others, so Cloud knows which one runs it.
health.iv_destNext_offline: Bring this machine back online; Cloud lists it as ready when it reports again.
health.iv_destNext_ready: Starting queues this incident for its investigation schedule. Connection is not confirmed; wait for the machine to claim it.
health.iv_destNext_setup_required: Complete the event-investigation schedule setup on this machine, then refresh this list.
health.iv_destNext_unknown: Cloud sent a state this page does not know ({raw}). Update this page or check the machine before choosing it.
health.iv_destNone: No machine is listed. Pair a machine, then create an investigation schedule on it and bind its Cloud webhook.
health.iv_destNoneReady: No listed machine can run an investigation yet. Follow the next step beside each one.
health.iv_destUnavailable: Cloud cannot list your machines right now. Try again in a moment.
health.iv_destUnsupported: This Cloud cannot yet say which machine runs investigations, so none can be started here.
health.iv_frozenNote: Cloud freezes revision {n} of this incident for the agent; nothing else is sent.
health.iv_gate_expired: This incident's evidence has passed retention, so it cannot be investigated.
health.iv_gate_limit: This incident has used all 5 investigations Cloud allows.
health.iv_gate_live: An investigation is already in progress; only one can run at a time.
health.iv_gate_older_revision: Investigations start from the latest revision. Open the latest one to start.
health.iv_gate_unavailable: Starting is off until Cloud can read this incident's investigations.
health.iv_gate_unknown_state: An investigation record could not be read, so whether one is running is unknown.
health.iv_gate_unsupported: Starting is off because this Cloud does not support investigations.
health.iv_next_accepted: Nothing to do yet. This card updates as the machine reports.
health.iv_next_canceled: Choose a webhook that is still active on an owned machine and start again.
health.iv_next_deadline_exceeded: Check the schedule's runs on that machine, then start again if needed.
health.iv_next_delivery_unknown: Reload in a moment. If it stays unknown, check the webhook's deliveries.
health.iv_next_dispatch_deferred: Wait. If it is still deferred near the deadline, check the schedule on that machine.
health.iv_next_leased: Nothing to do yet. This card updates as the machine reports.
health.iv_next_queued_unclaimed: Make sure the machine is online and runs a Clawdline version that takes investigations.
health.iv_next_recovery_not_observed: Deploy the fix and run the operation again. A fix that needs a restart recovers under a new incident.
health.iv_next_recovery_unverified: Wait for the operation to finish, then reload this incident.
health.iv_next_refused: Bind the webhook to an investigation schedule on that machine, then start again.
health.iv_next_report_missing: Check that the investigation schedule's instructions on that machine ask for a report.
health.iv_next_report_needs_evidence: Reproduce the problem or collect the missing records, then start again.
health.iv_next_report_verification_faile: Review the fix commit in the report before using it.
health.iv_next_running: Nothing to do yet. The result appears here when the task ends.
health.iv_next_task_not_successful: Open the task on that machine to see why, then start again.
health.iv_next_undelivered: Update Clawdline on that machine, check it is online, then start a new investigation.
health.iv_next_unknown: See the technical details below; this page may be older than Cloud.
health.iv_next_verified: Review it, then acknowledge the incident under Human review if you agree. The investigation does not close the incident.
health.iv_none: This incident has not been handed to an agent.
health.iv_onlyUnreadable: Cloud lists {n} investigation records, but this page could not read any of them.
health.iv_ref_bad_origin: Cloud refused the request because it did not come from this console's own address.
health.iv_ref_health_busy: Cloud is busy with this account's other reads. Try again in a moment.
health.iv_ref_health_store_unavailable: Cloud's investigation storage is not ready.
health.iv_ref_hook_unavailable: This webhook is not active, not yours, or its machine was revoked.
health.iv_ref_idempotency_conflict: This request key was already used for a different request. Start again.
health.iv_ref_incident_revision_moved: The incident gained a newer revision. Read it again, then start.
health.iv_ref_investigation_limit: This incident has used all 5 investigations Cloud allows.
health.iv_ref_investigation_open: An investigation is already in progress. It is shown above.
health.iv_ref_pro_required: Schedule webhooks need a Pro plan on your account.
health.iv_ref_webhook_queue_full: That machine already has too many deliveries waiting. Try again later.
health.iv_ref_webhook_rate_limited: This webhook was triggered too often. Try again in a minute.
health.iv_replayed: Cloud had already started this request; it is the same investigation.
health.iv_separateNote: A task that succeeds is not proof of recovery. Human review is separate: acknowledging closes the incident and changes no investigation.
health.iv_startedOk: Investigation started. Progress appears above as your machine reports it.
health.iv_unavailable: Cloud could not read this incident's investigations. Whether one is running is unknown, so a new one cannot be started now.
health.iv_unreadable: {n} investigation records could not be read by this page.
health.iv_unsupported: This Cloud does not support agent investigations yet, so none can be started here.
health.iv_why_accepted: Your machine accepted the investigation and is about to start the schedule.
health.iv_why_canceled: The delivery was canceled because the webhook was disabled, rotated or moved, or the machine was revoked.
health.iv_why_deadline_exceeded: The investigation passed its deadline without a final result.
health.iv_why_delivery_unknown: Cloud could not read the delivery, so the investigation's progress is unknown.
health.iv_why_dispatch_deferred: Your machine put the schedule off for now, for example because another run is still going.
health.iv_why_incident_unknown: Cloud could not read the incident, so recovery cannot be checked.
health.iv_why_leased: Your machine has taken the delivery and is reading the frozen evidence.
health.iv_why_none: Cloud gave no reason for this state.
health.iv_why_queued_unclaimed: Waiting for your machine to pick up the delivery.
health.iv_why_recovery_not_observed: The agent prepared a fix, but Cloud has not seen this operation recover since the investigation started.
health.iv_why_recovery_unverified: A recovery is underway, but no record yet proves it matches the agent's fix.
health.iv_why_refused: Your machine refused to run it. Usually this webhook is not bound to an investigation schedule there.
health.iv_why_report_missing: The task ended, but the agent sent no report, so nothing can be verified.
health.iv_why_report_needs_evidence: The agent needs more evidence than this incident holds.
health.iv_why_report_verification_failed: The agent prepared a change but could not verify it.
health.iv_why_running: The agent is investigating on your machine.
health.iv_why_task_not_successful: The agent's task ended without succeeding.
health.iv_why_undelivered: No machine took the investigation before it expired. An older Clawdline never runs one as an ordinary schedule.
health.iv_why_unknown: Cloud gave a reason this page does not recognise ({raw}).
health.iv_why_verified: A recovery record in the same operation, received after the start, matches the agent's fix.
health.lead_M01: What Cloud has stored: records, sources, stall groups, and how much of it can be seen.
health.lead_M02: Each machine's sources, boots and builds as received, with its stall groups and records.
health.lead_M03: Which producers report, what each stage proves, and what is not collected yet.
health.lead_M04: Every stored record of one operation, in producer order, with exact receive times.
health.lead_M05: Durable incidents Cloud opened, each as immutable revisions of frozen evidence, with no made-up cause.
health.lead_M06: Whether the monitoring itself is reporting: coverage, gaps, losses and bounds.
health.lead_evidence: A structured record for an agent, built only from what this page read.
health.locationsNote: Location codes for this build. A listed line is where a stage is recorded, not a root cause.
health.machinesNone: No machine is visible in this scope.
health.offlineNote: Offline is decided from presence expiry at the relay. Why the machine is offline is not inferred.
health.pausedNote: Paused at {time} UTC. The window and every age are frozen.
health.pr_clockNote: Observation times are the probe host's own clock and are not verified; receipt times are the Cloud's. Fresh means both within {window}.
health.pr_ev_clock_ahead: Observation dated {obs} after the read. The probe clock is unverified, so this is unknown.
health.pr_ev_delayed: Delayed upload: received {rec} ago but observed {obs} ago. Not current.
health.pr_ev_stale: Stale: last received {rec} ago. Unknown now, not offline.
health.pr_noTargets: No target results in the retained 24 h.
health.pr_off_body: No probe host is registered with the Cloud, so there is no evidence from outside its fault domain. This says nothing about whether the service is up or down.
health.pr_partial_producer_reported_loss: A probe host reported losing records before upload, so some checks are missing.
health.pr_partial_scan_cap: Only the newest probe records were read: counts are floors and loss counters are unknown.
health.pr_paused: Paused: not refreshing. A refresh still reads the latest evidence; probe evidence cannot be read as of an earlier time.
health.pr_provesTitle: What a result can and cannot show
health.pr_proves_api_readiness_route_ans: A 2xx shows the API readiness route answered from that viewpoint.
health.pr_proves_relay_health_route_answ: A 2xx shows the Relay health route answered from that viewpoint.
health.pr_readAt: Read at {time}. Every age below is measured at that moment.
health.pr_scopeNote: Latest retained probe evidence (up to 24 h), service scope. The Cloud's probe read takes no window, pin or account, so none of them apply here.
health.pr_silent_body: Registered hosts: {n}. No probe evidence was received in the retained 24 h. That is unknown, not offline.
health.pr_silent_title: Registered probe hosts have sent nothing
health.pr_uns_independence_verification: Whether a host is really independent
health.pr_uns_target_registry: Which targets should exist: a target never reported is absent
health.pr_unsupportedTitle: What the Cloud cannot say about probes
health.probeLead: A synthetic read from this viewer every {every}, at most one outstanding. It proves this viewer's viewpoint only and is excluded from user success and error figures.
health.probeNone: No probe result in this window.
health.scopeNote_cloud_operator: Relay, presence and service metadata. No owner machine detail and no content.
health.scopeNote_paired_owner: Your own machine's snapshot and this viewer's record. No other account.
health.selectionAbsent: Incident {id} is not in the loaded window. Your selection is kept.
health.servicesNone: No Cloud service rows are visible in this scope.
health.socketNote: A completed socket write means only that the local socket implementation accepted the bytes. It does not prove they were delivered, or that a viewer received or applied them.
health.st_bootOrderNote: Server order is when Cloud first accepted each boot, not when the boot started; a late upload or a clock jump makes them differ.

health.st_bundleUnsupported: This record is not an incident bundle. Each incident's audited export is on Incident investigation; owner-encrypted attachments are not built.
health.st_byEventUnknown: Split by event unknown: count cap reached
health.st_cause_unexplained: Unexplained: late, evicted, refused or never sent
health.st_clockBasis: Times are when Cloud received each record; order is the producer's sequence. Read at
health.st_copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text below and copy it instead.
health.st_evidenceNote: Built in this browser from the reads above only, field by field. It is not an incident bundle: an incident's audited export is on Incident investigation.
health.st_evidenceNothing: Nothing was read successfully, so there is nothing to copy.
health.st_evidenceSize: {kib} KiB of at most {max} KiB · {events} records · {groups} groups
health.st_evidenceTooLarge: The record would be {kib} KiB, over the {max} KiB bound. Narrow the window or open one trace.
health.st_fail_audit_unavailable: Cloud could not record the audit entry, so it returned nothing.

health.st_fail_body_too_large: The answer was larger than this page accepts.
health.st_fail_budget: The page's time budget ran out before this read finished.
health.st_fail_contract_bound: Cloud's answer had more rows than its own bound.
health.st_fail_contract_schema: Cloud answered in a version this page does not read.
health.st_fail_contract_shape: Cloud's answer did not match the contract.
health.st_fail_http_error: Cloud answered with an unexpected error.
health.st_fail_incident_expired: This incident's frozen evidence passed retention.
health.st_fail_incident_not_found: No such incident in the readable scope.
health.st_fail_invalid_request: Cloud refused the request's window or filter.
health.st_fail_machine_not_found: No such machine in the readable scope.
health.st_fail_rate_limited: Cloud is busy with this account's other reads. Try again in a moment.
health.st_fail_revision_cap: This incident has used all 16 revisions; Cloud cannot write another.
health.st_fail_revision_not_found: This incident has no such revision.
health.st_fail_server_deadline: Cloud could not answer within its deadline.
health.st_fail_timeout: The read took longer than its deadline.

health.st_fail_unsupported: Cloud does not support this yet.
health.st_fixtureBanner: Fixture data for development: task-owned examples, not read from Cloud. Nothing here describes a real machine.

health.st_gapsUnknown: Gaps were not computed for this read, so whether records are missing is unknown.
health.st_greason_sequence_gap_after: a later gap could hold its recovery
health.st_groupsRule: States derived by Cloud rule {rule} from content-free metadata, ordered by producer sequence. A state is not a root cause.
health.st_groupsUnknown: Groups were not derived for this read ({reason}), so stalls in this window are unknown.
health.st_incidentsUnsupported: Durable incidents are not built yet: Cloud answers that it cannot list or open them.

health.st_noGapsListed: No interior gaps among the retained records of this window.

health.st_notCollected: No source has sent evidence for this scope.

health.st_partStale: {part}: the last refresh failed ({reason}). Shown as read at {time}.
health.st_partial_page_bytes: the page reached its byte bound
health.st_partial_row_limit: more rows than one page holds

health.st_pinned: Paused: the window stays where it is.
health.st_presenceUnsupported: Cloud has no presence contract yet, so whether a machine is online is not known from this evidence.

health.st_wd_unverified_after_gap: unverified after a gap: not recovered
health.staleNote: The last refresh failed ({code}). Showing figures from {time} UTC; the current state is unknown.

health.tl_band_after_as_of: After this read: not reported yet
health.tl_band_gapUnknown: Records missing between these receipts (count unknown)
health.tl_bneckNone: No pending, failed or timed stage on the loaded page.
health.tl_bootSpan: Boot {boot}, generation {n}: first to last receipt
health.tl_elapsedNote: Bars are each stage's own elapsed time as the service measured it (the largest, for aggregate rows). They are not added up and are not end-to-end latency.
health.tl_gapsUnplaced: {n} listed gaps cannot be placed in time
health.tl_groupsNote: Each mark is a group's last receipt as {rule} derived it: the last observed transition, not how long it lasted.
health.tl_keyBoot: A boot's first to last receipt
health.tl_lastAfter: newest receipt is after the window
health.tl_lastBefore: newest receipt is before the window

health.tl_monoBack: producer monotonic clock went backwards {n}× against its own sequence
health.tl_noLanes: No record in this window was loaded.
health.tl_notCollectedNote: Each stays unknown until a producer reports it.
health.tl_problemNone: No loss, stall or slow group and no stale source in what was loaded. That is not a healthy verdict: there is no presence contract.
health.tl_problem_released_after_stall: Released after a stall in {n} groups
health.tl_qualityNotFull: Only what these reads returned. Never full coverage.
health.tl_seqNote: In producer sequence, not time: what Cloud received per source and boot, and the gaps it listed.
health.tl_seqUnknown: Sequence coverage was not computed for this read.
health.tl_sourcesNote: Each source's newest receipt on the window, and each boot from its first to its last receipt. Not every moment between receipts was observed.
health.tl_stagesLocal: From {n} of the {of} service records on the loaded page.
health.tl_stagesLocalMore: From {n} of the {of} service records loaded. Older pages are not included until they are loaded.
health.tl_traceNone: No stored record of this operation was loaded.
health.tl_traceNote: In producer order within each source and boot. Separate sources have unrelated clocks, so they are not merged into one order and no end-to-end time is computed.
health.tl_wallBack: producer wall clock went backwards {n}× (display only)
health.tr_absentUnknown: A bucket without a rollup is unknown, never zero traffic and never healthy.
health.tr_cellFilter: A cell filter is applied: totals cover only the matching cells.
health.tr_cellsDropped: {n} records did not fit their bucket's cell cap and are counted only in totals.
health.tr_clockBasis: Time is the Cloud's receipt minute; producer clocks are only counted when they differ by over 60 s, never used to place a record.
health.tr_countsBasis: Bars count accepted event records. Reported operations are the producers' own counts, at least when a record had none. Distinct operations are not aggregated.
health.tr_coveredFrom: Complete from {at}; earlier buckets are a floor or unknown.
health.tr_gap_after_as_of: after this read: not happened yet
health.tr_incomplete: older than the scanned range: a floor
health.tr_keyBad: bucket with a stall, slow, failed stage or loss
health.tr_lanesMore: {shown} of {total} sources are drawn; the table lists every one.
health.tr_lossUnverified: {lost} lost · {gaps} store gaps · {excluded} excluded · counters unverified
health.tr_moreSignals: {n} older buckets to investigate are not listed.
health.tr_noSeries: No rollup was stored for this window and scope. That is not zero traffic and not healthy: nothing was received to count.
health.tr_noSignals: No held bucket reports a stall, slow, failed stage or loss. Unknown buckets are not counted as clean.
health.tr_rawExpired: Raw records are kept for 24 h and are gone
health.tr_reason_cell_cap: some records exceeded the per-bucket cell cap
health.tr_reason_page_bytes: the answer reached the Cloud's page size
health.tr_reason_retention_floor: the window starts before the 30-day retention floor
health.tr_reason_rollup_refused: the Cloud refused some rollups in this window
health.tr_reason_row_limit: more than 50 sources; narrow by source or machine
health.tr_reason_scan_cap: more than 5,000 hour documents; only the newer ones were read
health.tr_refusalsMore: More refusal days exist than listed.
health.tr_restarts: {n} restarts (lines are not drawn across them)
health.tr_seriesMore: {shown} of {total} sources returned; narrow by source or machine.
health.tr_stageNone: No record in this window reported an elapsed time.
health.tr_stageNote: Each record's own elapsed for that stage (an aggregated service record carries its window's maximum). Stages are never added into an end-to-end time.
health.tr_unsupported: This Cloud does not keep minute rollups (aggregates: unsupported). No trend is shown, and none is implied.
health.tr_viewerNoErrors: The viewer sources held report no error class in this window.
health.tr_viewerNone: No viewer source reported in this window and scope.
health.tr_viewerNote: By the viewer's own error class, over held buckets only.
health.tr_wallSkew: {n} records whose producer clock was over 60 s from receipt
health.traceNotFound: This trace is not in the loaded window.
health.verdictNoIncident: No active incident in this window.
health.verdictUnknownNote: There is not enough evidence to say. This is not a healthy result.

settings.settingsCodexAutoNameHint: For each unnamed session, your chosen assistant runs one small turn using the session's request and latest reply. This uses that assistant's quota and never replaces a name you chose.
settings.settingsCodexDefaultEffortHint: Used for a new Codex session without its own effort choice. A child agent may still choose its own effort.
settings.settingsCompactWindowHint: Only for Claude sessions Clawdline opens — children, Root Assignments, handoffs — never Codex, never a session you opened. Past this many tokens of context the session replaces its history with a summary: every later call re-reads fewer tokens, which is where most of a long session's cost goes, but the summary can lose detail, files get read again, and each compaction takes about ten seconds. Empty leaves Claude Code alone; it then compacts near its own 1M window. A task can ask for its own. Takes effect at the next launch.
settings.settingsCompactWindowInvalid: A whole number of tokens from {min} to {max}, or empty for none.
settings.settingsDefaultModelHint: Used only when Clawdline opens a new session without another model choice. A child agent or one session may still choose its own model.
settings.settingsFollow: Show the selected session in the terminal
settings.settingsFollowHint: This selects that session's tab without bringing the terminal to the front. Otherwise, every press of Tab would move the keyboard away from the field you are typing in.
settings.settingsHooksHint: Once installed, Claude Code signals when a turn starts, ends, or needs your answer, without waiting for Clawdline to check again. The screen still determines each state; this only controls how quickly Clawdline checks it.
settings.settingsHooksLegacy: This file still has the older hook (clawdline/hook.sh). Claude Code runs it every turn, but this version does not read the note it leaves. Nothing breaks; it only runs an extra small command each time. To remove it, delete the entry containing clawdline/hook.sh from this file, or choose “Remove” in the older app's settings (which removes only its own entry).
settings.settingsHooksNone: This version does not install a hook. It reads session state from Claude Code's own state files.
settings.settingsHooksOff: Not installed — all states read from the screen
settings.settingsHooksOn: Installed — no session has reported yet
settings.settingsHooksStray: This file contains a clawdline-next/hook.sh entry, but this version does not read it.
settings.settingsHooksWhat: A hook is a command Claude Code runs at specific moments, registered in ~/.claude/settings.json. The older Clawdline hook leaves a note when a turn starts or ends, a permission dialog appears, or Claude Code asks a question. The older app then reads that session's screen right away. Without the hook, it checks every 20 seconds while the input box is hidden, so a permission request may take 20 seconds to appear in the menu bar. With the hook, it takes less than a second.
settings.settingsHooksWhy: Installing a hook changes Claude Code's settings file so it runs an extra command at eight points in every turn. This version cannot yet read those notes, so installation would only run unused commands. It does not offer installation or change ~/.claude/settings.json. The install button will appear once reading the notes is supported.
settings.settingsHooksWhyHead: Why is it absent from this version?
settings.settingsHooksWithout: Claude Code writes each session's state (busy, idle, waiting) to ~/.claude/sessions/. This version reads those files about every two seconds. The session list states, menu bar count, notch animation, and options shown when an answer is needed all come from there; no hook is needed. Compared with the older app's hook, a change may appear up to about two seconds later instead of within one second. Sessions without readable state files, such as Codex, are read from the terminal screen.
settings.settingsHotkeyHint: The default is ⌥Space. If another app (such as Alfred) uses the same combination, both may respond and Clawdline cannot detect that; choose another combination, or narrow “Where it works” below to terminals only.
settings.settingsHotkeyLegacy: The older Clawdline is also running and uses {combo}, so one press opens two input boxes. Quit the older app. If it starts at login, turn off “Launch at Login” in its menu.
settings.settingsHotkeyRefused: {combo} could not be registered (the operating system returned {status}). The ✳ in Clawdline's menu still opens the input box; press the button above to choose another combination.
settings.settingsHotkeySystem: {combo} is reserved by the operating system, so it was not registered. The ✳ in Clawdline's menu still opens the input box; press the button above to choose another combination.
settings.settingsHotkeyUnreadable: The hotkey “{spec}” in the settings file could not be read, so it was not registered. The ✳ in the menu bar can still open the input box; use the button above to record a new shortcut.
settings.settingsITermIntegrationHint: Off by default. While off, Clawdline does not detect, read or control iTerm2 or request its Automation permission. Enabling permits listing tabs, reading screens, sending input, and opening, showing or closing tabs, and may request macOS Automation permission. Existing installations must also opt in.
settings.settingsITermIntegrationUpgrade: This daemon does not support the iTerm2 consent switch. Update Clawdline on this machine to control all iTerm2 access. Its current access cannot be inferred from this page.
settings.settingsITermScanHint: Off: Clawdline stops asking iTerm2 which tabs it has, and does not read their screens or type into them. Opening a viewer tab for a tmux session and Show still send one Apple Event each. It takes effect on the next reading; nothing needs restarting.
settings.settingsNotchHint: Put a character by the camera. Turning this off draws nothing and does not create a window.
settings.settingsOrchestratorClose: After a child session reports back
settings.settingsOrchestratorCloseHint: Close its tab after it reports. Leave a timed-out tab open so you can inspect what happened.
settings.settingsOrchestratorEnabled: Let one session dispatch work to another
settings.settingsOrchestratorEnabledHint: A session with the clawdline skill can open a new tab, type instructions into it, then report back when it finishes. When this is off, new dispatches are blocked; tasks already running continue.
settings.settingsOrchestratorMaxHint: The default is five. The limit is per session, not per machine. Each child is a terminal tab with an assistant doing work in it.
settings.settingsOrchestratorNotify: Report back to the dispatching session
settings.settingsOrchestratorNotifyHint: When the task ends, type a line into that session.
settings.settingsOrchestratorPermission: How far a child can proceed on its own
settings.settingsOrchestratorPermissionH: Nobody watches a child's tab. A session that pauses for approval will remain there until it times out. Since a dispatched task runs commands and writes files, any setting short of the last one can stop it. A task may require stricter permission, but cannot exceed this setting.
settings.settingsPushDelivery: Notify me when a session reports delivery
settings.settingsPushDeliveryHint: Notify once per report; repeated reports of the same delivery stay quiet.
settings.settingsPushDeploy: Notify me when Cloud or app releases succeed
settings.settingsPushDeployHint: A separate notification follows each successful production check.
settings.settingsPushFanout: Notify me when a batch of dispatched tasks finishes
settings.settingsPushFanoutHint: Notify once for the whole batch, including the number of failures.
settings.settingsRemoteHint: When this is off, nothing outside this machine can reach it. When it is on, the session list is available on 127.0.0.1 — to a browser here, a phone connected through a tunnel, or a script. What it exposes is repository names, branches, and work titles, so it stays off until you turn it on.
settings.settingsRemoteServe: Let a browser or your phone view your sessions
settings.settingsRemoteWriteHint: Each device paired directly with this machine is read only or read and operate, chosen per device on the Devices page. Clawdline Cloud operation is a separate switch for this whole machine: clawdline cloud commands off.
settings.settingsReopen: Show and hide the input bar with the terminal
settings.settingsReopenHint: The input bar hides when you switch away from the terminal and returns when you switch back. Press Esc when you are done with it for now.
settings.settingsScopeHint: Leave this list empty to use the shortcut everywhere. Removing the last app turns on the switch above; turn it off to bring the list back. The settings file stores bundle IDs, and a manually edited list works too.
settings.settingsSessionTerminalConsentH: Automatic uses tmux while iTerm2 integration is off. With integration enabled, Automatic uses iTerm2 while it is open; with tmux installed, the Session runs in tmux and is shown in an iTerm2 tab. Explicit iTerm2 choices require enabled integration and a running iTerm2. iTerm2 (native tab) runs directly in its tab. tmux always uses tmux. The next Session follows this choice.
settings.settingsSessionTerminalHint: Automatic uses iTerm2 while it is open and tmux while it is not. Choosing iTerm2 names iTerm2: when it is closed the start is refused, even with a tmux server running. With tmux installed, both open the session in its own tmux session and show it in an iTerm2 tab, so reading and typing never wait on iTerm2. iTerm2 (native tab) runs the session in the tab itself, as before. tmux always opens in a tmux server, even with iTerm2 open. The next session follows this; nothing needs restarting.
settings.settingsSmartNotificationsHint: Use Haiku to explain what just finished. If generation fails, send the original notification.
settings.settingsStateHookHint: Whenever a session starts, finishes, or asks you something, Clawdline runs your program and passes the details through environment variables. This belongs in the settings file because it is an argv array, not a command line; a path with spaces remains one path.
settings.settingsTailscaleHint: When this machine and your phone are on the same tailnet, run tailscale serve --bg 7727 on this machine and enter its full name here, such as my-machine.your-tailnet.ts.net. It answers only while the switch above is on, and a device still pairs before it sees anything. Serve stays private to your tailnet; Funnel would make the address public, so do not use it.
settings.settingsVoiceLanguageHint: Whisper processes voice on this machine, no matter which browser or phone sent the recording. “Follow Clawdline” checks the language on the General tab first. If that is Automatic, it checks this machine's language and region. If neither specifies one, it uses the Clawdline interface language.

transparency.boundary: Clawdline additions only; excludes agent system prompts and existing user rules. Source excerpts are not translated.
transparency.card.antigravity-context.co: A managed native hook authenticates a saved launch with nonempty context
transparency.card.antigravity-context.ef: PREPARED records preparation. A later native system row must match the saved pre-response file boundary and exact context; PostInvocation or Stop can retain that proof without another model call. This does not create skill-applied receipts or change tool permissions.
transparency.card.antigravity-context.ho: The daemon verifies the private launch capability, native process, terminal and kernel workspace before preparing PreInvocation injectSteps. Policy-bearing launches also require current Project consent and the same live runtime owners. Unmanaged observations receive no Clawdline context.
transparency.card.antigravity-context.su: Uses the saved role prompt, Project memory, Board language and answer-Note rule. Exact resume preserves original skill paths and does not read current role, memory or language settings.

workflow.zeroReviewBody:
Run a zero-based review of this Project. Create an Epic to track it, then assign independent reviews from the relevant roles: product, UX, architecture, code quality, efficiency, documentation, and evidence.
Require evidence for every finding. Compare the current design with mature expert practice, and distinguish deliberate trade-offs from accumulated complexity.
Find confusing behavior, redundant steps or reads and writes, and missing capabilities.
Synthesize a report and a target workflow. Turn improvements into role-owned child items, and list decisions that need my input separately.
Collect shared facts once and include them in each review brief so reviewers do not repeat the same reading.

New dispatched tasks without an explicit permission mode use full permission, allowing the assistant to act without routine permission prompts.
Applies to future dispatches, including schedules using the machine default. Explicit task permissions take precedence. Running tasks and the assistant you opened yourself are unchanged.

transparency.card.gemini-acp-context.con: A configured personal ACP conversation has nonempty launch instructions
transparency.card.gemini-acp-context.sum: Captures the selected role and handbook, enabled-skill references, shared Project memory, Board language and answer-Note rule. Role selection uses the same existing Squad snapshot as other assistants.
transparency.card.gemini-acp-context.how: The first real user message carries one inline ACP resource and the original text. A blank open sends no model input. The owned and native conversation IDs bind the existing role actor; its private capability value is not included in instructions.
transparency.card.gemini-acp-context.eff: Resume keeps the original snapshot and never resends an interrupted message. An exact known flattened first replay is restored to the original user text; unknown formats are retained. Skill use needs its own receipt. This path does not install or bypass the separate native-hook policy.
